q: At its year end of 31 December 20X7, Navbahor Co had breached the conditions of a revenue grant received in 20X6, and it is probable that the government will demand repayment of $250,000. No repayment has yet been requested. How should this be dealt with in the financial statements for the year ended 31 December 20X7?
opt: Disclose a contingent liability only, as no demand has been received
Restate the 20X6 financial statements to remove the grant
Take no action until the government requests repayment
Recognise a liability for the repayment in the 20X7 financial statements, in accordance with IAS 37
ex: Agar grant'ni qaytarish majburiyati bo'lsa va repayment probable bo'lsa, IAS 37 bo'yicha provision (liability) tan olinadi. Shart buzilishi — o'tgan hodisa (past event), demak majburiyat hisobot sanasida mavjud; talab qilinishini kutish shart emas. Contingent liability faqat repayment possible (probable emas) bo'lganda. O'tgan yil restate qilinmaydi.

q:
Extracts from Termez Co's financial statements show deferred income from government grants (current and non-current combined) of $2,400,000 at 1 January 20X8 and $3,100,000 at 31 December 20X8. Grant income of $500,000 was released to profit or loss during the year. No grants were repaid.
What amount of cash was received from government grants in 20X8? Enter your answer in $000.
ex:
Deferred income T-account ($000):
b/f 2,400 + received (X) − released 500 = c/f 3,100
X = 3,100 + 500 − 2,400 = 1,200.
Current va non-current qismlarni qo'shib olish kerak — aks holda javob noto'g'ri chiqadi.

q: Kattaqo'rg'on Co prepares its statement of cash flows using the indirect method. During the year, $180,000 of deferred grant income was released to profit or loss. How should this be dealt with in calculating cash generated from operations?
opt: Added to profit before tax, as it is a non-cash item similar to depreciation
Shown as a cash inflow within investing activities
Deducted from profit before tax, as it is non-cash income
Shown as a cash inflow within financing activities
ex:
Grant release — P/L'dagi non-cash income (naqd pul avval, grant olinganda kirgan). Indirect method'da profit before tax'ga qo'shilgan bo'lgani uchun uni ayirish kerak (depreciation esa non-cash expense — qo'shiladi, grant release teskari).
Grant uchun olingan haqiqiy naqd pul esa alohida ko'rsatiladi (odatda investing activities'da).

q: Ohangaron Co had deferred income from capital grants of $900,000 at 1 January 20X9 and $1,260,000 at 31 December 20X9. During 20X9, $120,000 was released to profit or loss. Which TWO of the following will appear in Ohangaron Co's statement of cash flows for 20X9?
opt: An addition of $120,000 in reconciling profit before tax to cash generated from operations
Cash received from government grants of $360,000 within investing activities
Cash received from government grants of $360,000 within financing activities
A deduction of $120,000 in reconciling profit before tax to cash generated from operations
Cash received from government grants of $480,000 within investing activities
ex:
Release 120k — non-cash income → operating activities'da profit'dan ayiriladi.
Olingan naqd pul ($000): b/f 900 + X − 120 = c/f 1,260 → X = 1,260 + 120 − 900 = 480 → $480,000, investing activities'da (capital grant — aktiv sotib olish bilan bog'liq).
$360,000 — faqat balans o'zgarishi (1,260 − 900), release hisobga olinmagan.

q: In a statement of cash flows prepared using the indirect method, the release of deferred grant income to profit or loss is added back to profit before tax because it is a non-cash item.
ex: Noto'g'ri. Grant release — non-cash income, u profit'ni oshirgan, lekin cash kirmagan. Shuning uchun u profit before tax'dan ayiriladi (qo'shilmaydi). Qo'shiladigan non-cash item'lar — depreciation kabi non-cash expense'lar.

q: Guzor Co received a grant of $600,000 towards a new machine and uses the deferred income method. How is the receipt of the $600,000 recorded at the date it is received?
opt: Dr Cash $600,000, Cr Deferred income $600,000
Dr Cash $600,000, Cr Property, plant and equipment $600,000
Dr Deferred income $600,000, Cr Cash $600,000
Dr Cash $600,000, Cr Other income $600,000
ex:
Deferred income method: grant olinganda Dr Cash / Cr Deferred income (liability). Keyin har yili Dr Deferred income / Cr P/L (release).
Cr PPE — netting off method yozuvi. Cr Other income — grant'ni darhol daromad qilish (noto'g'ri).

q: On 1 January 20X9 Beruniy Co bought a machine for $1,000,000 and received a government grant of $250,000 towards it. The machine has a five-year life and nil residual value. Beruniy Co uses the deferred income method. Which THREE of the following will appear in its financial statements for the year ended 31 December 20X9?
opt: A non-current liability for deferred income of $200,000
Depreciation expense of $200,000
Grant income of $50,000
A current liability for deferred income of $50,000
Property, plant and equipment at cost of $750,000
ex:
Depreciation = 1,000,000 / 5 = $200,000 (to'liq cost bo'yicha).
Grant income = 250,000 / 5 = $50,000.
Deferred income balans = 250,000 − 50,000 = $200,000: current $50,000, non-current $150,000.
Cost $750,000 — netting off method; non-current $200,000 — split qilinmagan jami balans.

q: Nukus Co changes from the deferred income method to the netting off method for all of its grants related to assets. How should this change be accounted for?
opt: As the correction of a prior period error
As a change in accounting estimate, applied prospectively
As a change in accounting policy, applied retrospectively under IAS 8
No accounting is needed, as both methods give the same profit each year
ex: IAS 20 ikki usulni ruxsat beradi — ulardan birini tanlash accounting policy. Shu sababli usulni o'zgartirish — change in accounting policy, IAS 8 bo'yicha retrospective qo'llanadi (SOFP taqdimoti o'zgaradi: PPE va liabilities). Sof foyda bir xil bo'lsa ham, SOFP'dagi summalar farq qiladi.

q:
Olmaliq Co prepares financial statements to 31 December 20X7 and uses the deferred income method for grants related to assets.
  • (i) On 1 April 20X7 Olmaliq Co bought a machine for $6 million with a ten-year useful life and received a government grant of $1.5 million towards it.
  • (ii) On 1 July 20X7 Olmaliq Co received $480,000 from the government on condition that it keeps 200 employees at its Angren site for two years. It expects to meet the condition. The whole $480,000 was credited to revenue.
  • (iii) On 1 January 20X5 Olmaliq Co received a grant of $800,000 towards plant with an eight-year life. On 31 December 20X7 Olmaliq Co breached the conditions and the full grant became repayable.
What is the grant income to be recognised in profit or loss for 20X7 in respect of the machine grant in (i)? Enter your answer in $000, to one decimal place.

Olmaliq Co prepares financial statements to 31 December 20X7 and uses the deferred income method for grants related to assets.
  • (i) On 1 April 20X7 Olmaliq Co bought a machine for $6 million with a ten-year useful life and received a government grant of $1.5 million towards it.
  • (ii) On 1 July 20X7 Olmaliq Co received $480,000 from the government on condition that it keeps 200 employees at its Angren site for two years. It expects to meet the condition. The whole $480,000 was credited to revenue.
  • (iii) On 1 January 20X5 Olmaliq Co received a grant of $800,000 towards plant with an eight-year life. On 31 December 20X7 Olmaliq Co breached the conditions and the full grant became repayable.
What is the non-current liability in respect of the machine grant in (i) at 31 December 20X7?
ex:
Balans = 1,500,000 − 112,500 = $1,387,500.
Current = 20X8 dagi release = $150,000.
Non-current = 1,387,500 − 150,000 = $1,237,500.
$1,387,500 — split qilinmagan; $1,350,000 — to'liq yil release qilingan deb xato hisoblangan.

q:
Olmaliq Co prepares financial statements to 31 December 20X7 and uses the deferred income method for grants related to assets.
  • (i) On 1 April 20X7 Olmaliq Co bought a machine for $6 million with a ten-year useful life and received a government grant of $1.5 million towards it.
  • (ii) On 1 July 20X7 Olmaliq Co received $480,000 from the government on condition that it keeps 200 employees at its Angren site for two years. It expects to meet the condition. The whole $480,000 was credited to revenue.
  • (iii) On 1 January 20X5 Olmaliq Co received a grant of $800,000 towards plant with an eight-year life. On 31 December 20X7 Olmaliq Co breached the conditions and the full grant became repayable.
By how much is Olmaliq Co's profit for 20X7 overstated as a result of the treatment of the grant in (ii)? Enter your answer in $000.
ex:
Revenue grant 24 oylik shart davriga taqsimlanadi: oyiga 480,000 / 24 = $20,000.
20X7: 6 oy (iyul–dekabr) → to'g'ri income = 20,000 × 6 = $120,000.
Tan olingan 480,000 → profit ortiqcha = 480,000 − 120,000 = $360,000 → 360 ($000).
Tuzatish: Dr Revenue 480,000 / Cr Deferred income 360,000 (240,000 current, 120,000 non-current) / Cr Other income (yoki staff costs) 120,000. Grant IFRS 15 revenue emas, shuning uchun revenue'dan butunlay chiqariladi.

q:
Olmaliq Co prepares financial statements to 31 December 20X7 and uses the deferred income method for grants related to assets.
  • (i) On 1 April 20X7 Olmaliq Co bought a machine for $6 million with a ten-year useful life and received a government grant of $1.5 million towards it.
  • (ii) On 1 July 20X7 Olmaliq Co received $480,000 from the government on condition that it keeps 200 employees at its Angren site for two years. It expects to meet the condition. The whole $480,000 was credited to revenue.
  • (iii) On 1 January 20X5 Olmaliq Co received a grant of $800,000 towards plant with an eight-year life. On 31 December 20X7 Olmaliq Co breached the conditions and the full grant became repayable.
Which TWO of the following are acceptable ways of presenting the grant income from (ii) that relates to 20X7?
opt: As a deduction from staff costs
Within revenue from contracts with customers
As a gain in other comprehensive income
As other income in profit or loss
ex: Revenue (income) grant: IAS 20 bo'yicha yoki other income sifatida, yoki bog'liq xarajatdan (staff costs) ayirib ko'rsatiladi. Grant — mijoz bilan shartnoma emas, shuning uchun IFRS 15 revenue emas; OCI ham qo'llanmaydi.

q:
Olmaliq Co prepares financial statements to 31 December 20X7 and uses the deferred income method for grants related to assets.
  • (i) On 1 April 20X7 Olmaliq Co bought a machine for $6 million with a ten-year useful life and received a government grant of $1.5 million towards it.
  • (ii) On 1 July 20X7 Olmaliq Co received $480,000 from the government on condition that it keeps 200 employees at its Angren site for two years. It expects to meet the condition. The whole $480,000 was credited to revenue.
  • (iii) On 1 January 20X5 Olmaliq Co received a grant of $800,000 towards plant with an eight-year life. On 31 December 20X7 Olmaliq Co breached the conditions and the full grant became repayable.
After the release for 20X7 has been recorded, what expense should be recognised in profit or loss for the repayment of the grant in (iii)? Enter your answer in $000.
ex:
Release: 800,000 / 8 = $100,000 yiliga; 20X5–20X7 = 3 yil = $300,000.
31.12.20X7 da deferred income = 800,000 − 300,000 = $500,000.
Qaytariladi $800,000 → avval deferred income 500,000 ishlatiladi, ortiqcha = 800,000 − 500,000 = $300,000 → P/L expense (300 $000).
Repayment probable/majburiy bo'lgani uchun liability 20X7 da tan olinadi.

q:
Navoiy Co prepares financial statements to 30 June 20X9 and uses the deferred income method for grants related to assets. At 1 July 20X8 total deferred income (current and non-current) was $3,200,000. During the year to 30 June 20X9:
  • $640,000 was released to profit or loss in respect of grants held at 1 July 20X8;
  • on 1 January 20X9 Navoiy Co received a new grant of $1,440,000 towards equipment costing $4,800,000, bought that day, with a six-year useful life and nil residual value.
No grants were repaid. Depreciation and grant releases are time-apportioned.
What amount should be released to profit or loss in the year in respect of the new grant? Enter your answer in $000.

Navoiy Co prepares financial statements to 30 June 20X9 and uses the deferred income method for grants related to assets. At 1 July 20X8 total deferred income (current and non-current) was $3,200,000. During the year to 30 June 20X9:
  • $640,000 was released to profit or loss in respect of grants held at 1 July 20X8;
  • on 1 January 20X9 Navoiy Co received a new grant of $1,440,000 towards equipment costing $4,800,000, bought that day, with a six-year useful life and nil residual value.
No grants were repaid. Depreciation and grant releases are time-apportioned.
What is the total deferred income balance (current and non-current) at 30 June 20X9? Enter your answer in $000.
ex: b/f 3,200,000 + yangi grant 1,440,000 − eski grant release 640,000 − yangi grant release 120,000 = $3,880,000 → 3,880 ($000).

q:
Navoiy Co prepares financial statements to 30 June 20X9 and uses the deferred income method for grants related to assets. At 1 July 20X8 total deferred income (current and non-current) was $3,200,000. During the year to 30 June 20X9:
  • $640,000 was released to profit or loss in respect of grants held at 1 July 20X8;
  • on 1 January 20X9 Navoiy Co received a new grant of $1,440,000 towards equipment costing $4,800,000, bought that day, with a six-year useful life and nil residual value.
No grants were repaid. Depreciation and grant releases are time-apportioned.
How should the total grant release of $760,000 be dealt with in Navoiy Co's statement of cash flows (indirect method)?
opt: Deducted from profit before tax in arriving at cash generated from operations
Shown as a cash outflow within investing activities
Added to profit before tax in arriving at cash generated from operations
Ignored, as it has no effect on the statement of cash flows
ex: Jami release = 640,000 + 120,000 = $760,000 — non-cash income, profit'ni oshirgan. Indirect method'da profit before tax'dan ayiriladi. Grant uchun olingan haqiqiy naqd pul ($1,440,000) esa alohida — investing activities'da inflow sifatida.

q:
Navoiy Co prepares financial statements to 30 June 20X9 and uses the deferred income method for grants related to assets. At 1 July 20X8 total deferred income (current and non-current) was $3,200,000. During the year to 30 June 20X9:
  • $640,000 was released to profit or loss in respect of grants held at 1 July 20X8;
  • on 1 January 20X9 Navoiy Co received a new grant of $1,440,000 towards equipment costing $4,800,000, bought that day, with a six-year useful life and nil residual value.
No grants were repaid. Depreciation and grant releases are time-apportioned.
If Navoiy Co had instead deducted the new grant from the cost of the equipment, what would the depreciation charge on the equipment have been for the year ended 30 June 20X9?
ex:
Netting off: net cost = 4,800,000 − 1,440,000 = $3,360,000.
Depreciation = 3,360,000 / 6 × 6/12 = $280,000.
Tekshiruv: deferred income method'da depreciation 400,000 − release 120,000 = 280,000 — sof ta'sir bir xil.

q:
Navoiy Co prepares financial statements to 30 June 20X9 and uses the deferred income method for grants related to assets. At 1 July 20X8 total deferred income (current and non-current) was $3,200,000. During the year to 30 June 20X9:
  • $640,000 was released to profit or loss in respect of grants held at 1 July 20X8;
  • on 1 January 20X9 Navoiy Co received a new grant of $1,440,000 towards equipment costing $4,800,000, bought that day, with a six-year useful life and nil residual value.
No grants were repaid. Depreciation and grant releases are time-apportioned.
Navoiy Co could switch to the netting off method for new grants only, without this being treated as a change in accounting policy, because IAS 20 permits both methods.
ex: Noto'g'ri. IAS 20 ruxsat bergan ikki usuldan birini tanlash — accounting policy. O'xshash grantlar uchun izchil (consistent) qo'llanishi kerak; usulni o'zgartirish IAS 8 bo'yicha change in accounting policy hisoblanadi (va faqat relevant/reliable ma'lumot bersa ruxsat etiladi).

q: Which of the following is a qualifying asset as defined by IAS 23 Borrowing Costs?
opt: A hotel being built by Samarqand Resorts Co that is expected to take 22 months to complete
Bottled mineral water produced daily in large quantities by Chortoq Co
A delivery van purchased by Sayhun Co that was ready for use on the day it was delivered
An investment in the ordinary shares of a listed company held by Oqtepa Co
ex: Qualifying asset — o'z maqsadli foydalanishi yoki sotuvi uchun tayyor bo'lishiga substantial period of time (sezilarli uzoq vaqt) kerak bo'ladigan aktiv. 22 oy quriladigan mehmonxona — aynan shunday. Har kuni katta miqdorda ishlab chiqariladigan inventory, sotib olinganda darhol ishlatishga tayyor mashina va financial asset (aksiyalar) qualifying asset emas.

q: Which TWO of the following would normally be qualifying assets under IAS 23?
opt: An internally developed software platform expected to take two years to complete (meeting the IAS 38 criteria)
A completed office building purchased and occupied immediately
A power station that will take three years to construct
A portfolio of corporate bonds
Packaged snacks manufactured in large volumes each week
ex: IAS 23 bo'yicha qualifying asset PPE, intangible asset, investment property yoki inventory bo'lishi mumkin — asosiysi tayyor bo'lishi uchun uzoq vaqt talab qilsin. Power station (3 yil qurilish) va 2 yil davom etadigan ichki software development (intangible) — qualifying. Tayyor holda sotib olingan ofis binosi darhol ishlatishga tayyor, financial assets va qisqa muddatda takroriy ishlab chiqariladigan inventory — qualifying emas.

q: An asset that is ready for its intended use or sale at the date it is acquired is not a qualifying asset under IAS 23.
ex: To'g'ri. Qualifying asset ta'rifining mohiyati — tayyor bo'lishi uchun sezilarli vaqt kerak. Sotib olinganda tayyor bo'lgan aktiv uchun capitalisation davri yo'q, shuning uchun unga oid borrowing costs P/L'ga expense qilinadi.

q: Which of the following is NOT a borrowing cost as defined by IAS 23?
opt: Interest expense calculated using the effective interest method
Interest on lease liabilities recognised under IFRS 16
Dividends paid on ordinary share capital
Interest charged on a bank overdraft
ex: Borrowing costs — entity'ning qarz mablag' olish bilan bog'liq interest va boshqa xarajatlari: effective interest method bo'yicha hisoblangan interest (IFRS 9), lease liability bo'yicha interest (IFRS 16) va h.k. Ordinary shares bo'yicha dividendlar — equity'ga to'lov (distribution), qarz xarajati emas, shuning uchun borrowing cost hisoblanmaydi.

q: Which of the following describes the treatment of borrowing costs required by IAS 23?
opt: Entities may choose, as an accounting policy, to capitalise or expense borrowing costs on qualifying assets
Borrowing costs directly attributable to a qualifying asset must be capitalised; all other borrowing costs are expensed
All borrowing costs must be recognised as an expense in the period in which they are incurred
Borrowing costs must be capitalised on any non-current asset financed by a loan
ex: IAS 23 (revised) bo'yicha qualifying asset'ga directly attributable borrowing costs majburiy ravishda capitalise qilinadi (tanlov yo'q). Qolgan barcha borrowing costs yuzaga kelgan davrda expense sifatida P/L'ga olinadi.

q: Under IAS 23 an entity may adopt an accounting policy of expensing all borrowing costs, including those that relate to qualifying assets.
ex: Noto'g'ri. Eski IAS 23 da bunday tanlov bor edi, hozirgi IAS 23 da yo'q: qualifying asset'ga to'g'ridan-to'g'ri tegishli borrowing costs capitalise qilinishi shart.

q: Which THREE conditions must all be met before an entity begins to capitalise borrowing costs on a qualifying asset?
opt: Activities necessary to prepare the asset for its intended use are in progress
The loan has been fully drawn down
The asset is available for use
Borrowing costs are being incurred
Expenditure for the asset is being incurred
ex: Capitalisation uchala shart birga bajarilgan kundan boshlanadi: (1) aktiv uchun expenditure qilinmoqda; (2) borrowing costs yuzaga kelmoqda; (3) aktivni tayyorlash uchun zarur faoliyat (activities) davom etmoqda. Aktivning foydalanishga tayyor bo'lishi — bu capitalisation tugashi sharti; kreditning to'liq olinishi shart emas.

q:
Nurafshon Co has a year end of 31 December 20X4. It received a loan specifically to build a new distribution centre on 1 February 20X4. It paid for the site on 1 March 20X4, and physical construction work began on 1 May 20X4. No other activities relating to the project took place before 1 May 20X4.
From which date should Nurafshon Co begin to capitalise borrowing costs?
opt: 1 February 20X4
1 March 20X4
1 January 20X4
1 May 20X4
ex: Capitalisation uchala shart bajarilganda boshlanadi. 1 fevral — faqat borrowing costs bor. 1 mart — expenditure ham bor (yer uchun to'lov), lekin qurilish faoliyati hali yo'q (yer shunchaki ushlab turilibdi — bu activity emas). 1 may — uchala shart bajarildi. Javob: 1 May 20X4. Fevral–aprel interest'i P/L'ga finance cost.

q: Borrowing costs incurred while land is simply being held, with no development activity taking place, qualify for capitalisation.
ex: Noto'g'ri. Yerni shunchaki ushlab turish (holding) — aktivni tayyorlash uchun zarur activity emas. Faqat rivojlantirish ishlari (texnik/ma'muriy ishlar, masalan permit olish, yoki fizik qurilish) boshlangandan keyin capitalisation mumkin.

q:
Bekobod Co obtained a specific loan on 1 January 20X6 to build a factory. From 1 February 20X6 its architects and lawyers worked on obtaining building permits, and the company paid their fees as they were incurred. Physical construction started on 1 June 20X6.
From which date should borrowing costs be capitalised?
opt: 1 June 20X6
1 January 20X6
1 February 20X6
The date the factory is completed
ex: IAS 23 bo'yicha 'activities necessary to prepare the asset' faqat fizik qurilish emas — u qurilishdan oldingi texnik va ma'muriy ishlarni ham (masalan building permits olish) o'z ichiga oladi. 1 fevraldan: expenditure (fees) bor, borrowing costs bor, activity (permit ishlari) bor → capitalisation 1 February 20X6 dan boshlanadi. 1 yanvar — hali activity va expenditure yo'q.

q: In which of the following situations should capitalisation of borrowing costs be suspended?
opt: Construction is halted for four months because of an industrial dispute
Work pauses for two weeks while concrete foundations set, as is normal in the process
Physical work pauses while engineers carry out substantial technical design work on the next phase
Minor decoration work is still outstanding after the asset is substantially complete
ex: Capitalisation faqat uzoq muddatli (extended) to'xtash davrida suspend qilinadi — masalan, mehnat nizosi (industrial dispute) sababli 4 oy ish to'xtashi. Texnik va ma'muriy ishlar davom etayotgan bo'lsa, yoki kechikish jarayonning zaruriy qismi bo'lsa (beton qotishi, mintaqada odatiy mavsumiy suv toshqini) — suspend qilinmaydi. Kichik bezak ishlari esa cessation masalasi, suspension emas.

q: Which TWO of the following would NOT require capitalisation of borrowing costs to be suspended?
opt: An indefinite pause while the directors reconsider whether to continue the project
A six-month strike by construction workers
A two-month delay caused by high water levels that are expected every year in the region and were built into the construction schedule
A five-month halt because the entity ran out of funds
A period in which no physical building took place but engineers were carrying out substantial technical work on the design
ex: Suspension — faqat active development uzoq muddat to'xtatilganda. Suspend QILINMAYDI: (1) jarayonning zaruriy qismi bo'lgan vaqtinchalik kechikish (masalan, qurilish hududida har yili bo'ladigan va kutilgan suv toshqini davri); (2) fizik ish yo'q, lekin sezilarli texnik/ma'muriy ishlar davom etmoqda. Moliyalash tugab qolgani sababli 5 oy to'xtash, 6 oylik strike va loyiha qayta ko'rib chiqilguncha muddatsiz to'xtatish — extended suspension, capitalisation to'xtatiladi.

q:
Qarshi Mall Co was building a shopping centre. The building was substantially complete on 31 October 20X5, apart from minor decoration of the entrance hall which was finished on 20 December 20X5. The centre opened to the public on 1 February 20X6.
On which date should capitalisation of borrowing costs cease?
opt: 20 December 20X5
31 October 20X5
31 December 20X5
1 February 20X6
ex: Capitalisation aktivni maqsadli foydalanishga tayyorlash uchun zarur deyarli barcha (substantially all) faoliyat tugaganda to'xtaydi. Kichik bezak ishlari qolgan bo'lsa ham aktiv 31 oktyabrda substantially complete. Haqiqiy ochilish sanasi (1 fevral) ahamiyatsiz. Javob: 31 October 20X5; undan keyingi interest P/L'ga.

q:
Yashnobod Co is building a business park made up of five separate office blocks, each of which can be let to tenants while construction continues on the other blocks. Block 1 was completed on 30 April 20X7; the other blocks are still under construction at the year end.
How should borrowing costs relating to Block 1 be treated after 30 April 20X7?
opt: They should continue to be capitalised until the whole business park is complete
They should be capitalised until Block 1 is first let to a tenant
They should be transferred to the cost of the remaining blocks under construction
They should be expensed, because Block 1 can be used while construction continues on the other blocks
ex: Agar qualifying asset qismlari alohida bitib, qolgan qismlar qurilayotgan paytda har biri alohida foydalanishga yaroqli bo'lsa, capitalisation har bir qism uchun u substantially complete bo'lganda to'xtaydi. Block 1 alohida ijaraga berilishi mumkin → 30 apreldan keyin unga tegishli borrowing costs P/L'ga expense. Butun park tugashini kutish kerak emas (bu faqat qismlar alohida ishlatib bo'lmaydigan holatda, masalan zavodning ketma-ket bosqichlari).

q:
On 1 January 20X3 Guliston Co took out a $6,000,000 8% loan specifically to build a new warehouse. Construction began on 1 January 20X3 and was still in progress at the year end, 31 December 20X3. No funds were temporarily invested.
What amount of borrowing costs should be capitalised for the year ended 31 December 20X3? Enter your answer in $, to the nearest whole number.
ex:
Specific loan, capitalisation butun yil (12 oy):
$6,000,000 × 8% × 12/12 = $480,000.

q:
Jizzax Cement Co received a $12,000,000 7% loan on 1 January 20X3 to finance a new kiln. Construction started on 1 March 20X3 and the kiln was ready for use on 30 November 20X3. The year end is 31 December 20X3.
What amount of borrowing costs should be capitalised? Enter your answer in $000, to the nearest whole number.
ex:
Capitalisation davri: 1 mart – 30 noyabr = 9 oy (yanvar–fevral qurilish yo'q; dekabr aktiv tayyor).
$12,000,000 × 7% × 9/12 = $630,000 = $630k. Qolgan 3 oy interest'i ($210,000) P/L'ga.

q:
Termiz Logistics Co has a 31 March year end. On 1 April 20X5 it received a $9,000,000 6% loan to build a cold-storage depot. Construction ran from 1 April 20X5 to 31 January 20X6. Because the funds were not needed immediately, $4,000,000 was invested at 3% per annum from 1 April 20X5 to 31 July 20X5.
What amount should be capitalised as borrowing costs for the year ended 31 March 20X6? Enter your answer in $, to the nearest whole number.
ex:
Capitalisation davri: 1 aprel – 31 yanvar = 10 oy.
Interest: $9,000,000 × 6% × 10/12 = $450,000
Minus investment income (capitalisation davri ichida, 4 oy): $4,000,000 × 3% × 4/12 = ($40,000)
Capitalise: $410,000.

q:
Chirchiq Chemicals Co (year end 31 December 20X4) borrowed $10,000,000 at 9% on 1 January 20X4, specifically to build a new processing plant. Construction started on 1 March 20X4 and was still in progress at 31 December 20X4. $3,000,000 of the loan was invested at 4% per annum from 1 January to 30 June 20X4.
What amount of borrowing costs should be capitalised for 20X4? Enter your answer in $, to the nearest whole number.
ex:
Capitalisation davri: 1 mart – 31 dekabr = 10 oy.
Interest: $10,000,000 × 9% × 10/12 = $750,000
Investment income faqat capitalisation davri ichidagi qismi ayriladi: 1 mart – 30 iyun = 4 oy: $3,000,000 × 4% × 4/12 = ($40,000)
Capitalise: $710,000.
Yanvar–fevral daromadi ($20,000) capitalisation boshlanishidan oldin — P/L'ga investment income.

q:
Kosonsoy Textiles Co (year end 31 December 20X5) took out an $8,000,000 7.5% loan on 1 January 20X5 to construct a new mill. Construction began on 1 April 20X5 and continued beyond the year end. $2,000,000 was invested at 3% from 1 January to 31 May 20X5.
What finance cost should be recognised in profit or loss for 20X5 in respect of this loan?
ex: Interest capitalisation boshlanishidan oldingi davr (1 yanvar – 31 mart, 3 oy) P/L'ga: $8,000,000 × 7.5% × 3/12 = $150,000. Aprel–dekabr interest'i ($450,000) capitalise qilinadi. Investment income finance cost'dan ayrilmaydi: yanvar–mart daromadi ($15,000) P/L'da alohida investment income, aprel–may daromadi ($10,000) esa capitalise qilinadigan summadan ayriladi.

q:
Andijon Motors Co (year end 31 December 20X6) borrowed $15,000,000 at 8% on 1 January 20X6 to build an assembly plant. Construction started on 1 January 20X6 and continued past the year end. Work stopped completely from 1 May to 31 July 20X6 because of an industrial dispute.
What borrowing costs should be capitalised for 20X6? Enter your answer in $000, to the nearest whole number.
ex:
Industrial dispute — extended suspension, 3 oy (may, iyun, iyul) capitalisation to'xtatiladi.
Capitalisation oylari: 12 − 3 = 9.
$15,000,000 × 8% × 9/12 = $900,000 = $900k. 3 oylik interest ($300,000) P/L'ga.

q:
On 1 January 20X5 Buxoro Plaza Co began building a supermarket. The site cost $4,000,000 and construction costs were $7,000,000. The project was financed by an $11,000,000 10% loan taken out on 1 January 20X5. The supermarket was completed on 30 September 20X5 and opened on 1 December 20X5.
What total amount should be recognised in property, plant and equipment for the supermarket (before depreciation) at 31 December 20X5? Enter your answer in $000, to the nearest whole number.
ex:
Borrowing costs faqat 1 yanvar – 30 sentyabr (9 oy) uchun: $11,000,000 × 10% × 9/12 = $825,000.
PPE = site $4,000,000 + construction $7,000,000 + borrowing costs $825,000 = $11,825,000 = $11,825k. Oktyabr–dekabr interest'i P/L'ga (ochilish sanasi 1 dekabr ahamiyatsiz).
subtopic: Effective interest and total asset cost
topic: Effective interest and total asset cost

q:
Olmaliq Co completed a new laboratory building on 30 September 20X8 and it became available for use on 1 October 20X8. Construction costs were $8,000,000 and borrowing costs of $400,000 were correctly capitalised. The building has a useful life of 40 years and nil residual value. The year end is 31 December 20X8.
What depreciation charge should be recognised for the year ended 31 December 20X8? Enter your answer in $, to the nearest whole number.
ex:
Capitalise qilingan borrowing costs aktiv cost'ining bir qismi → u ham depreciate qilinadi.
Cost = $8,000,000 + $400,000 = $8,400,000.
Depreciation available for use sanasidan (1 oktyabr), 3 oy: $8,400,000 / 40 × 3/12 = $52,500.
subtopic: Effective interest and total asset cost
topic: Effective interest and total asset cost

q:
On 1 January 20X4 Zarafshon Co issued a $5,000,000 loan note at par, with a 5% coupon, to finance the construction of a hotel. The loan note is redeemable at a premium, giving an effective interest rate of 6.5%. Construction continued throughout 20X4.
What amount of borrowing costs should be capitalised for the year ended 31 December 20X4?
ex:
IAS 23 bo'yicha borrowing costs IFRS 9 dagi effective interest method bilan hisoblanadi (finance cost = amortised cost × effective rate), coupon emas.
$5,000,000 × 6.5% × 12/12 = $325,000. Coupon ($250,000) — naqd to'lov; farq ($75,000) loan carrying amount'iga qo'shiladi.
subtopic: Effective interest and total asset cost
topic: Effective interest and total asset cost

q:
Karshi Foods Co has the following general borrowings outstanding throughout the year: a $4,000,000 loan at 5% and a $6,000,000 loan at 10%.
What is the capitalisation rate to be applied to expenditure on a qualifying asset funded from these general borrowings? Enter your answer as a percentage, to one decimal place.
ex:
Capitalisation rate = jami borrowing costs / jami general borrowings (weighted average).
($4,000,000 × 5% + $6,000,000 × 10%) / $10,000,000 = ($200,000 + $600,000) / $10,000,000 = 8.0%. Oddiy o'rtacha (7.5%) noto'g'ri.

q:
Navoiy Mining Co has three general loans outstanding for the whole year: $2,000,000 at 6%, $5,000,000 at 8% and $3,000,000 at 11%.
What is the weighted average capitalisation rate? Enter your answer as a percentage, to one decimal place.

During the year Urgut Co had $3,000,000 of 5% loans and $1,000,000 of 9% loans outstanding, neither of which was taken out for a specific purpose. It built a new packing shed costing $900,000, funded from these borrowings. The expenditure was incurred at the start of construction and the shed took six months to complete.
To the nearest thousand, what borrowing costs should be capitalised? Enter your answer in $000.
ex:
Capitalisation rate = ($150,000 + $90,000) / $4,000,000 = 6%.
Capitalise = expenditure × rate × davr = $900,000 × 6% × 6/12 = $27,000 ≈ $27k. Diqqat: rate jami qarzga emas, aktivga sarflangan summaga qo'llanadi.

q:
Denov Co funded the construction of a new workshop from its general borrowings, which carry a weighted average rate of 7.2%. It spent $2,500,000 on the workshop at the start of construction, and construction took eight months.
What borrowing costs should be capitalised?
ex:
General borrowings: aktivga sarflangan summa × capitalisation rate × capitalisation davri.
$2,500,000 × 7.2% × 8/12 = $120,000.

q:
Kattaqo'rg'on Co (year end 31 December 20X5) built a warehouse between 1 January and 31 December 20X5, funding it entirely from general borrowings with a capitalisation rate of 9%. Expenditure on the warehouse was incurred as follows:
DateAmount
1 January 20X5$1,000,000
1 April 20X5$2,000,000
1 October 20X5$1,500,000
What borrowing costs should be capitalised for 20X5? Enter your answer in $, to the nearest whole number.
ex:
Har bir expenditure sarflangan kundan boshlab capitalise qilinadi:
$1,000,000 × 9% × 12/12 = $90,000
$2,000,000 × 9% × 9/12 = $135,000
$1,500,000 × 9% × 3/12 = $33,750
Jami = $258,750.

q: The amount of borrowing costs that an entity capitalises from general borrowings during a period must not exceed the total borrowing costs it incurred during that period.
ex: To'g'ri. IAS 23 cheklovi: general borrowings'dan capitalise qilingan summa shu davrda haqiqatda yuzaga kelgan borrowing costs'dan oshmasligi kerak. Imputed (xayoliy) interest capitalise qilinmaydi.

q:
Xonqa Co has the following borrowings outstanding for the whole year:
LoanAmountRate
Bank loan (general)$10,000,0006%
Bonds (general)$4,000,0009%
Loan taken specifically to build a hotel still under construction$5,000,00012%
What capitalisation rate should Xonqa Co apply to expenditure on a new factory funded from its general borrowings (to two decimal places)?
ex:
Capitalisation rate'ga faqat general borrowings kiradi; hali qurilayotgan qualifying asset uchun olingan specific loan chiqarib tashlanadi.
($10,000,000 × 6% + $4,000,000 × 9%) / $14,000,000 = $960,000 / $14,000,000 = 6.86%.
Specific loan'ni qo'shsangiz 8.21% chiqadi — noto'g'ri. Oddiy o'rtacha (7.50%) ham noto'g'ri.

q: When a qualifying asset is financed from an entity's general borrowings, how is the amount of borrowing costs to be capitalised determined?
opt: By capitalising all interest incurred on general borrowings during the construction period
By applying a weighted average capitalisation rate to the expenditure on the asset
By applying the highest interest rate on any of the entity's loans to the expenditure on the asset
By applying the entity's cost of equity to the expenditure on the asset
ex: General borrowings holatida aktivga sarflangan summa (expenditure) weighted average capitalisation rate'ga ko'paytiriladi (capitalisation davri bo'yicha time-apportion). Jami qarzning barcha interest'i yoki eng yuqori stavka ishlatilmaydi.

q:
Throughout the year ended 31 December 20X6, Shahrisabz Co had a general loan of $6,000,000 at 8%. It also had a general loan of $4,000,000 at 12%, which was repaid on 30 June 20X6. No other borrowings existed.
What is the capitalisation rate for 20X6, based on the borrowing costs incurred and the weighted average borrowings outstanding? Enter your answer as a percentage, to one decimal place.
ex:
Qarz yil davomida o'zgarsa, rate = davr borrowing costs / weighted average qarz.
Borrowing costs: $6,000,000 × 8% = $480,000; $4,000,000 × 12% × 6/12 = $240,000. Jami = $720,000.
Weighted average qarz: $6,000,000 + $4,000,000 × 6/12 = $8,000,000.
Rate = $720,000 / $8,000,000 = 9.0%.

q:
Bulung'ur Co (year end 31 December 20X7) began constructing a grain silo on 1 January 20X7, funded from general borrowings with a capitalisation rate of 10%. It spent $2,000,000 on 1 January 20X7 and $1,200,000 on 1 July 20X7. The silo was completed on 30 September 20X7.
What borrowing costs should be capitalised for 20X7?

Zomin Resorts Co (year end 31 December 20X8) is building a spa hotel. It took out a $5,000,000 7% loan specifically for the project on 1 January 20X8, and construction ran throughout 20X8. The whole specific loan was spent on the project and none of it was temporarily invested. On 1 July 20X8 it spent a further $2,000,000 on the hotel, funded from its general borrowings, which have a capitalisation rate of 9%.
What total borrowing costs should be capitalised for 20X8? Enter your answer in $, to the nearest whole number.
ex:
Specific va general qismlar alohida hisoblanadi:
Specific: $5,000,000 × 7% × 12/12 = $350,000
General: $2,000,000 × 9% × 6/12 = $90,000
Jami = $440,000.

q: Interest on a loan used to build a qualifying asset was initially charged to finance costs. Which journal entry is needed to capitalise the interest correctly?
opt: Dr Property, plant and equipment; Cr Finance costs
Dr Retained earnings; Cr Property, plant and equipment
Dr Finance costs; Cr Property, plant and equipment
Dr Property, plant and equipment; Cr Revaluation surplus
ex: Interest dastlab finance costs'ga (P/L) yozilgan. Uni aktiv cost'iga o'tkazish uchun: Dr PPE (asset under construction), Cr Finance costs. Natijada PPE oshadi, P/L xarajati kamayadi (profit oshadi).

q: During the capitalisation period, an entity earned interest income by temporarily investing part of a loan taken out specifically to build a qualifying asset. How should that income be treated?
opt: It is recognised as investment income in profit or loss
It is recognised in other comprehensive income
It is added to the cost of the qualifying asset
It is deducted from the borrowing costs eligible for capitalisation
ex: Specific borrowings bo'yicha capitalisation davri ichida vaqtincha investitsiyadan olingan daromad capitalise qilinadigan borrowing costs'dan ayriladi (net off). U alohida income sifatida P/L'ga ham, OCI'ga ham yozilmaydi. (Capitalisation boshlanishidan oldingi daromad esa P/L'ga.)

q: Which TWO of the following must an entity disclose under IAS 23?
opt: The remaining term of each loan
The capitalisation rate used to determine the amount of borrowing costs eligible for capitalisation
The name of each lender
The fair value of each loan used to finance qualifying assets
The amount of borrowing costs capitalised during the period
ex: IAS 23 disclosure talablari qisqa: (1) davr mobaynida capitalise qilingan borrowing costs summasi; (2) capitalise qilinadigan summani aniqlash uchun ishlatilgan capitalisation rate. Kreditor nomi, loan fair value va har bir loan'ning muddati IAS 23 talabi emas.

q: Payariq Co expensed borrowing costs of $300,000 that should have been capitalised on a factory still under construction at the year end. What is the effect of this error on the financial statements?
opt: Profit is understated by $300,000 but property, plant and equipment is correctly stated
Profit and property, plant and equipment are both overstated by $300,000
Profit and property, plant and equipment are both understated by $300,000
There is no effect on profit because the cash paid is the same
ex: Capitalise qilinishi kerak bo'lgan $300,000 P/L'ga yozilgan: finance costs $300,000 ga oshib ketgan → profit $300,000 ga kam; aktivga qo'shilmagan → PPE $300,000 ga kam. Tuzatish: Dr PPE $300,000, Cr Finance costs $300,000. Aktiv hali tugamagan — depreciation ta'siri yo'q.

q: Borrowing costs capitalised as part of the cost of a building are depreciated over the useful life of the building once it is available for use.
ex: To'g'ri. Capitalise qilingan borrowing costs aktiv cost'ining bir qismi bo'ladi va aktiv available for use bo'lgan kundan boshlab uning useful life'i davomida depreciation orqali P/L'ga o'tadi.

q: Tashkent Towers Co capitalises borrowing costs on its qualifying assets, whereas a competitor, identical in every other respect, incorrectly expenses them. Compared with the competitor, which of the following is true for Tashkent Towers Co during the construction period?
opt: The interest it pays in cash will be lower
Its finance costs recognised in profit or loss will be lower
Its future depreciation charges will be lower
Its property, plant and equipment carrying amount will be lower
ex: Capitalisation natijasida qurilish davrida P/L'dagi finance costs kamroq bo'ladi (bir qismi aktivga o'tadi). Naqd to'langan interest bir xil — buxgalteriya usuli naqd pulga ta'sir qilmaydi. PPE carrying amount yuqoriroq, kelajakdagi depreciation ham yuqoriroq bo'ladi.

q:
Marg'ilon Silk Co (year end 31 December 20X6) took out a $5,000,000 6% loan on 1 January 20X6 to build a dyeing plant. Construction started on 1 March 20X6 and the plant was ready for use on 31 October 20X6.
What interest on the loan should be expensed in profit or loss for 20X6?
ex:
Jami interest $300,000. Capitalisation 1 mart – 31 oktyabr = 8 oy ($200,000).
P/L: yanvar–fevral (2 oy) + noyabr–dekabr (2 oy) = 4 oy → $5,000,000 × 6% × 4/12 = $100,000.

q:
Angren Coal Co (year end 31 December 20X6) received a $6,000,000 10% loan on 1 January 20X6 to build a conveyor system. Construction began on 1 February 20X6 and continued past the year end, except that all work was halted from 1 June to 31 August 20X6 while a contractor dispute was resolved. $2,500,000 of the loan was invested at 4.8% from 1 January to 31 March 20X6.
What borrowing costs should be capitalised for 20X6? Enter your answer in $, to the nearest whole number.
ex:
Capitalisation oylari: fevral–may (4) + sentyabr–dekabr (4) = 8 oy (iyun–avgust — suspension).
Interest: $6,000,000 × 10% × 8/12 = $400,000
Investment income capitalisation davri ichida: fevral–mart = 2 oy: $2,500,000 × 4.8% × 2/12 = ($20,000)
Capitalise: $380,000. Yanvar daromadi ($10,000) P/L'ga.

q:
Samarqand Tiles Co (year end 31 December) began constructing a kiln on 1 July 20X1, financed by a $4,000,000 9% loan taken out on that date. The kiln was completed on 31 March 20X2.
What borrowing costs should be capitalised in the year ended 31 December 20X2? Enter your answer in $, to the nearest whole number.
ex:
20X2 yilda capitalisation faqat 1 yanvar – 31 mart (3 oy) davom etadi.
$4,000,000 × 9% × 3/12 = $90,000. Aprel–dekabr interest'i ($270,000) P/L'ga. (20X1 da 6 oy — $180,000 capitalise qilingan edi.)

q: For a qualifying asset financed by a loan taken out specifically for that asset, which amount is capitalised under IAS 23?
opt: The actual borrowing costs incurred during the capitalisation period, less investment income on the temporary investment of those borrowings
The full amount of the loan principal
The actual borrowing costs incurred for the whole year, regardless of when construction started
The weighted average cost of all of the entity's borrowings applied to the expenditure
ex: Specific borrowings uchun: capitalisation davridagi haqiqiy borrowing costs minus shu mablag'larni vaqtincha investitsiya qilishdan olingan daromad. Weighted average rate faqat general borrowings uchun. Loan'ning o'zi (principal) liability, aktiv cost'i emas.

q:
Ohangaron Co (year end 31 December 20X3) built a new depot. Construction costs of $3,600,000 were incurred, financed by a $3,000,000 8% loan taken out on 1 January 20X3. Construction ran from 1 January to 31 August 20X3. $1,000,000 of the loan was invested at 3% from 1 January to 30 April 20X3.
What is the total cost of the depot to be included in property, plant and equipment? Enter your answer in $000, to the nearest whole number.
subtopic: Effective interest and total asset cost
topic: Effective interest and total asset cost

q: Yunusobod Homes Co builds residential apartment blocks for sale. Each block takes about two years to complete and is financed by a specific loan. How should the borrowing costs incurred during construction be treated?
opt: They are recognised in other comprehensive income until the apartments are sold
They are expensed, because inventories can never be qualifying assets
They are capitalised as part of property, plant and equipment
They are capitalised as part of the cost of inventories
ex: Qurilishi 2 yil davom etadigan va sotish uchun mo'ljallangan apartment blocks — inventory bo'lgan qualifying asset (tayyorlash uchun substantial period talab qiladi). Borrowing costs inventory cost'iga capitalise qilinadi va sotilganda cost of sales orqali P/L'ga o'tadi. PPE emas, chunki aktiv sotish uchun.

q: Chust Co is constructing a new factory over 18 months, entirely funded from its own cash reserves. It has no borrowings. The finance director suggests capitalising a notional interest charge based on the return the cash could have earned. What is the correct treatment?
opt: No borrowing costs are capitalised, because no borrowing costs have been incurred
Notional interest should be capitalised at the entity's cost of capital
Notional interest should be capitalised at the market rate of interest
Notional interest should be recognised in other comprehensive income
ex: IAS 23 faqat entity haqiqatda yuzaga kelgan borrowing costs'ni capitalise qilishga ruxsat beradi. Qarzi bo'lmagan entity'da borrowing cost yo'q — notional/imputed interest yoki opportunity cost capitalise qilinmaydi. Factory qualifying asset bo'lsa ham capitalise qiladigan narsa yo'q.

q: Investment income earned on specific borrowings before capitalisation of borrowing costs has commenced is deducted from the amount capitalised.
ex: Noto'g'ri. Faqat capitalisation davri ichida olingan investment income capitalise qilinadigan summadan ayriladi. Capitalisation boshlanishidan oldingi (yoki tugagandan keyingi) daromad P/L'ga investment income sifatida olinadi.

q: Which THREE of the following statements about IAS 23 Borrowing Costs are correct?
opt: Capitalisation ceases when substantially all activities necessary to prepare the asset are complete
A weighted average capitalisation rate is applied to expenditure funded from general borrowings
Borrowing costs directly attributable to a qualifying asset must be capitalised
Borrowing costs must be capitalised on any non-current asset financed by a loan
Capitalisation begins as soon as expenditure on the asset is incurred, whether or not work has started
ex: To'g'ri: (1) qualifying asset'ga tegishli borrowing costs capitalise qilinishi shart; (2) capitalisation aktiv substantially complete bo'lganda tugaydi; (3) general borrowings uchun weighted average capitalisation rate ishlatiladi. Noto'g'ri: 'loan bilan moliyalangan har qanday non-current asset' — faqat qualifying asset; capitalisation faqat expenditure boshlanganda emas, uchala shart bajarilganda boshlanadi.

q: Which THREE of the following would be included in the borrowing costs capitalised on a qualifying asset funded by a specific loan note?
opt: The coupon interest on the loan note for the capitalisation period
Dividends paid to ordinary shareholders during the construction period
The amortisation of issue costs, as part of the effective interest charge for the capitalisation period
Repayments of the loan principal made during the construction period
The amortisation of the premium payable on redemption, as part of the effective interest charge
ex: Borrowing costs IFRS 9 effective interest method bo'yicha o'lchanadi: finance cost = coupon + issue costs amortisation + redemption premium amortisation (hammasi effective rate ichida). Capitalisation davri ichidagi shu finance cost capitalise qilinadi. Loan principal'ni to'lash — liability'ni kamaytirish, xarajat emas. Ordinary dividends — equity distribution.

q:
Guliston Steel Co (year end 31 December 20X8) received a specific loan on 1 March 20X8. Construction work on the qualifying asset started on 1 January 20X8, funded initially from cash, and continued throughout the year.
For which period should borrowing costs on the specific loan be capitalised in 20X8?
opt: 1 January to 31 December 20X8 (12 months)
1 January to 28 February 20X8 (2 months)
1 March to 31 December 20X8 (10 months)
No capitalisation, because construction began before the loan was received
ex: Capitalisation uchala shart bajarilganda boshlanadi. Qurilish va expenditure 1 yanvardan bor, lekin borrowing costs faqat 1 martdan (loan olingan kun) yuzaga keladi. Demak specific loan bo'yicha capitalisation: 1 mart – 31 dekabr = 10 oy.

q:
Qibray Co took out a $7,500,000 8% loan specifically to construct a data centre. Construction ran throughout the whole year. The company invested surplus funds temporarily and earned investment income of $45,000 during the year. The finance director proposes to capitalise the gross interest of $600,000 and show the $45,000 as investment income in profit or loss.
What is the effect of the finance director's proposal compared with the correct treatment?
opt: Both property, plant and equipment and profit are understated by $45,000
Both property, plant and equipment and profit are overstated by $45,000
There is no effect, because the net amount is the same
Property, plant and equipment is overstated by $45,000, but profit is correct
ex: To'g'ri usul: capitalise = $600,000 − $45,000 = $555,000; P/L'da investment income yo'q. Direktor taklifi: PPE $600,000 (ya'ni $45,000 ga ortiqcha) va P/L'da $45,000 income (profit $45,000 ga ortiqcha). Demak ikkalasi ham $45,000 ga overstated.

q: Which TWO of the following would cause capitalisation of borrowing costs on a qualifying asset to cease?
opt: Substantially all the activities necessary to prepare the asset for its intended use are complete
One part of the asset, which can be used while work continues on the other parts, is completed (for that part)
Work pauses for ten days while concrete sets, as is normal for the process
The completed asset is formally opened by the directors three months after it was ready
The entity reaches its reporting date while construction is still in progress
ex: Capitalisation to'xtaydi: (1) aktivni tayyorlash uchun zarur deyarli barcha faoliyat tugaganda (substantially complete); (2) alohida foydalanish mumkin bo'lgan qism tugaganda — shu qism uchun. Aktivning rasmiy ochilishi, yil oxiri yoki beton qotishi kabi odatiy qisqa kechikish capitalisation'ni to'xtatmaydi.

q: Which TWO of the following are effects, in the year of construction, of capitalising borrowing costs on a qualifying asset rather than expensing them?
opt: The carrying amount of property, plant and equipment is higher
Equity is lower
Interest paid in cash is lower
Depreciation in future years is lower
Finance costs in profit or loss are lower
ex: Capitalisation: (1) P/L'dagi finance costs kamayadi (profit oshadi); (2) PPE carrying amount oshadi. Naqd to'langan interest o'zgarmaydi; equity (retained earnings) kamaymaydi, aksincha oshadi; kelajakdagi depreciation esa kamaymaydi, oshadi.

q: Chorvoq Co is calculating the capitalisation rate for expenditure on a new warehouse funded from its general borrowings. Which THREE of the following should be included in the calculation?
opt: A loan taken out specifically to build a hotel that is still under construction
A loan originally taken out specifically for a hotel that is now complete, which remains outstanding
A bank overdraft used for general working capital
Ordinary share capital issued during the year
A five-year bank loan taken out for general business purposes
ex: Capitalisation rate'ga entity'ning general borrowings'lari kiradi: umumiy bank loan va umumiy maqsaddagi overdraft. IAS 23 (2019 dagi o'zgarish) bo'yicha specific loan, u bilan bog'liq aktiv foydalanishga tayyor bo'lgandan keyin ham qaytarilmagan bo'lsa, general borrowings'ga qo'shiladi. Hali qurilayotgan boshqa qualifying asset uchun olingan specific loan chiqarib tashlanadi. Ordinary share capital — qarz emas.

q:
Registan Hotels Co has a year end of 31 December 20X7. On 1 January 20X7 it received a $24,000,000 6% loan specifically to build a new hotel. Construction began on 1 March 20X7. Work was halted from 1 July to 30 September 20X7 because of a prolonged dispute with the main contractor. As the funds were not needed immediately, $8,000,000 was invested at 3% per annum from 1 January to 30 April 20X7. The hotel was substantially complete on 30 November 20X7 and opened to guests on 1 February 20X8.

Which TWO of the following statements about Registan Hotels Co's borrowing costs are correct?
opt: Capitalisation ceases on 1 February 20X8 when the hotel opens
Capitalisation commences on 1 January 20X7 because the loan was received on that date
All investment income earned from 1 January to 30 April 20X7 is deducted from the amount capitalised
Capitalisation is suspended from 1 July to 30 September 20X7
Capitalisation commences on 1 March 20X7
ex: To'g'ri: (1) capitalisation 1 martda boshlanadi — shu kuni uchala shart bajarildi; (2) iyul–sentyabr — contractor bilan uzoq nizo, extended suspension → capitalisation to'xtatiladi. Noto'g'ri: capitalisation 1 fevral 20X8 (ochilish) da emas, 30 noyabr 20X7 da tugaydi; yanvar–fevral investment income P/L'ga, ayrilmaydi; loan 1 yanvarda olingan bo'lsa ham qurilish yo'q edi.

q:
Registan Hotels Co has a year end of 31 December 20X7. On 1 January 20X7 it received a $24,000,000 6% loan specifically to build a new hotel. Construction began on 1 March 20X7. Work was halted from 1 July to 30 September 20X7 because of a prolonged dispute with the main contractor. As the funds were not needed immediately, $8,000,000 was invested at 3% per annum from 1 January to 30 April 20X7. The hotel was substantially complete on 30 November 20X7 and opened to guests on 1 February 20X8.

What amount of borrowing costs should be capitalised in the cost of the hotel for the year ended 31 December 20X7? Enter your answer in $000, to the nearest whole number.
ex:
Capitalisation oylari: mart–iyun (4) + oktyabr–noyabr (2) = 6 oy.
Interest: $24,000,000 × 6% × 6/12 = $720,000
Investment income capitalisation davri ichida: mart–aprel (2 oy): $8,000,000 × 3% × 2/12 = ($40,000)
Capitalise = $680,000 = $680k.

q:
Registan Hotels Co has a year end of 31 December 20X7. On 1 January 20X7 it received a $24,000,000 6% loan specifically to build a new hotel. Construction began on 1 March 20X7. Work was halted from 1 July to 30 September 20X7 because of a prolonged dispute with the main contractor. As the funds were not needed immediately, $8,000,000 was invested at 3% per annum from 1 January to 30 April 20X7. The hotel was substantially complete on 30 November 20X7 and opened to guests on 1 February 20X8.

What interest on the loan should be recognised as a finance cost in profit or loss for the year ended 31 December 20X7? Enter your answer in $000, to the nearest whole number.
ex:
Jami interest: $24,000,000 × 6% = $1,440,000.
Capitalise qilinadigan gross interest (6 oy) = $720,000.
P/L finance cost = $1,440,000 − $720,000 = $720,000 = $720k (yanvar–fevral, iyul–sentyabr, dekabr = 6 oy).

q:
Registan Hotels Co has a year end of 31 December 20X7. On 1 January 20X7 it received a $24,000,000 6% loan specifically to build a new hotel. Construction began on 1 March 20X7. Work was halted from 1 July to 30 September 20X7 because of a prolonged dispute with the main contractor. As the funds were not needed immediately, $8,000,000 was invested at 3% per annum from 1 January to 30 April 20X7. The hotel was substantially complete on 30 November 20X7 and opened to guests on 1 February 20X8.

What investment income should be recognised in profit or loss for the year ended 31 December 20X7?
ex: Jami investment income: $8,000,000 × 3% × 4/12 = $80,000. Mart–aprel qismi ($40,000) capitalise qilinadigan summadan ayriladi. Yanvar–fevral (capitalisation boshlanishidan oldin) qismi P/L'ga: $8,000,000 × 3% × 2/12 = $40,000.

q:
Registan Hotels Co has a year end of 31 December 20X7. On 1 January 20X7 it received a $24,000,000 6% loan specifically to build a new hotel. Construction began on 1 March 20X7. Work was halted from 1 July to 30 September 20X7 because of a prolonged dispute with the main contractor. As the funds were not needed immediately, $8,000,000 was invested at 3% per annum from 1 January to 30 April 20X7. The hotel was substantially complete on 30 November 20X7 and opened to guests on 1 February 20X8.

On which date should capitalisation of borrowing costs on the hotel cease?
opt: 31 December 20X7
1 February 20X8
30 November 20X7
30 September 20X7
ex: Capitalisation aktiv substantially complete bo'lganda to'xtaydi — 30 November 20X7. Ochilish sanasi (1 fevral 20X8) va yil oxiri ahamiyatsiz.

q:
Chimgan Engineering Co has a year end of 30 June 20X5. It built a new manufacturing facility between 1 July 20X4 and 31 March 20X5, funding it entirely from general borrowings. The facility was available for use on 1 April 20X5 and has a useful life of 25 years with nil residual value. Expenditure on the facility was: $3,000,000 on 1 July 20X4, $4,000,000 on 1 October 20X4 and $2,000,000 on 1 January 20X5. Chimgan's general borrowings, all outstanding for the whole year, were: $10,000,000 bank loan at 7%, $6,000,000 bonds at 9% and $4,000,000 loan notes at 10%.

What is the capitalisation rate to be applied to expenditure on the facility? Enter your answer as a percentage, to one decimal place.

Chimgan Engineering Co has a year end of 30 June 20X5. It built a new manufacturing facility between 1 July 20X4 and 31 March 20X5, funding it entirely from general borrowings. The facility was available for use on 1 April 20X5 and has a useful life of 25 years with nil residual value. Expenditure on the facility was: $3,000,000 on 1 July 20X4, $4,000,000 on 1 October 20X4 and $2,000,000 on 1 January 20X5. Chimgan's general borrowings, all outstanding for the whole year, were: $10,000,000 bank loan at 7%, $6,000,000 bonds at 9% and $4,000,000 loan notes at 10%.

What borrowing costs should be capitalised in the cost of the facility for the year ended 30 June 20X5? Enter your answer in $, to the nearest whole number.

Chimgan Engineering Co has a year end of 30 June 20X5. It built a new manufacturing facility between 1 July 20X4 and 31 March 20X5, funding it entirely from general borrowings. The facility was available for use on 1 April 20X5 and has a useful life of 25 years with nil residual value. Expenditure on the facility was: $3,000,000 on 1 July 20X4, $4,000,000 on 1 October 20X4 and $2,000,000 on 1 January 20X5. Chimgan's general borrowings, all outstanding for the whole year, were: $10,000,000 bank loan at 7%, $6,000,000 bonds at 9% and $4,000,000 loan notes at 10%.

The borrowing costs Chimgan Engineering Co capitalises for the year cannot exceed the total borrowing costs of $1,640,000 it incurred on its general borrowings in the year.
ex: To'g'ri. General borrowings'dan capitalise qilinadigan summa davrdagi haqiqiy borrowing costs'dan oshmasligi kerak. Bu yerda capitalise qilingan $389,500 jami $1,640,000 dan kam — cheklov buzilmaydi.

q:
Chimgan Engineering Co has a year end of 30 June 20X5. It built a new manufacturing facility between 1 July 20X4 and 31 March 20X5, funding it entirely from general borrowings. The facility was available for use on 1 April 20X5 and has a useful life of 25 years with nil residual value. Expenditure on the facility was: $3,000,000 on 1 July 20X4, $4,000,000 on 1 October 20X4 and $2,000,000 on 1 January 20X5. Chimgan's general borrowings, all outstanding for the whole year, were: $10,000,000 bank loan at 7%, $6,000,000 bonds at 9% and $4,000,000 loan notes at 10%.

What depreciation charge should be recognised on the facility for the year ended 30 June 20X5 (to the nearest dollar)?
ex:
Cost = expenditure $9,000,000 + borrowing costs $389,500 = $9,389,500.
Depreciation 1 apreldan (3 oy): $9,389,500 / 25 × 3/12 = $93,895.
