  • On 1 July 20X6 it bought a magazine publishing title from a competitor for $1,200,000; useful life 10 years.
  • A consultant has valued Harlow Co's own newspaper masthead, created by Harlow Co over 30 years, at $3 million.
  • On 1 July 20X6 it acquired 100% of Kite Co for $5,600,000. The fair value of Kite Co's identifiable net assets as recorded was $4,100,000. Kite Co also had an internally generated brand, not recorded by Kite Co, reliably valued at $700,000, and a customer list that cannot be measured reliably.
  • On 1 July 20X6 it bought a regional broadcasting licence for $2,000,000 with a 5-year life. Such licences are freely traded in an active market and Harlow Co uses the revaluation model for them. At 30 June 20X7 the licence's fair value was $1,900,000.
  • It spent $150,000 training editorial staff on new editing software.
What is the carrying amount of the purchased publishing title at 30 June 20X7?
ex:
Sotib olingan publishing title — alohida sotib olingan intangible, cost model (publishing rights'ni revalue qilish taqiqlangan).
Amortisation = 1,200,000 / 10 = 120,000
Carrying amount = 1,200,000 − 120,000 = $1,080,000. Javob: B.

q:
Harlow Co, a media company, prepares financial statements to 30 June 20X7. During the year:
  • On 1 July 20X6 it bought a magazine publishing title from a competitor for $1,200,000; useful life 10 years.
  • A consultant has valued Harlow Co's own newspaper masthead, created by Harlow Co over 30 years, at $3 million.
  • On 1 July 20X6 it acquired 100% of Kite Co for $5,600,000. The fair value of Kite Co's identifiable net assets as recorded was $4,100,000. Kite Co also had an internally generated brand, not recorded by Kite Co, reliably valued at $700,000, and a customer list that cannot be measured reliably.
  • On 1 July 20X6 it bought a regional broadcasting licence for $2,000,000 with a 5-year life. Such licences are freely traded in an active market and Harlow Co uses the revaluation model for them. At 30 June 20X7 the licence's fair value was $1,900,000.
  • It spent $150,000 training editorial staff on new editing software.
Which of the following should be recognised as separate intangible assets in Harlow Co's consolidated statement of financial position at 30 June 20X7?
opt: The magazine publishing title
Harlow Co's newspaper masthead
Kite Co's brand
The regional broadcasting licence
Kite Co's customer list
ex:
A — sotib olingan publishing title ✔.
B — Harlow'ning o'z masthead'i: internally generated → hech qachon tan olinmaydi ✘.
C — Kite'ning brand'i: acquisition'da ishonchli baholangan → alohida intangible ✔.
D — broadcasting licence ✔ (revaluation model).
E — Kite'ning customer list'i: ishonchli o'lchanmaydi → goodwill ichida ✘. Javob: A, C, D.

q:
Harlow Co, a media company, prepares financial statements to 30 June 20X7. During the year:
  • On 1 July 20X6 it bought a magazine publishing title from a competitor for $1,200,000; useful life 10 years.
  • A consultant has valued Harlow Co's own newspaper masthead, created by Harlow Co over 30 years, at $3 million.
  • On 1 July 20X6 it acquired 100% of Kite Co for $5,600,000. The fair value of Kite Co's identifiable net assets as recorded was $4,100,000. Kite Co also had an internally generated brand, not recorded by Kite Co, reliably valued at $700,000, and a customer list that cannot be measured reliably.
  • On 1 July 20X6 it bought a regional broadcasting licence for $2,000,000 with a 5-year life. Such licences are freely traded in an active market and Harlow Co uses the revaluation model for them. At 30 June 20X7 the licence's fair value was $1,900,000.
  • It spent $150,000 training editorial staff on new editing software.
What goodwill arises on the acquisition of Kite Co? Enter your answer in $, to the nearest whole number.
ex:
Identifiable net assets = 4,100,000 + brand 700,000 = 4,800,000 (customer list ishonchli o'lchanmaydi → alohida emas)
Goodwill = 5,600,000 − 4,800,000 = $800,000.

q:
Harlow Co, a media company, prepares financial statements to 30 June 20X7. During the year:
  • On 1 July 20X6 it bought a magazine publishing title from a competitor for $1,200,000; useful life 10 years.
  • A consultant has valued Harlow Co's own newspaper masthead, created by Harlow Co over 30 years, at $3 million.
  • On 1 July 20X6 it acquired 100% of Kite Co for $5,600,000. The fair value of Kite Co's identifiable net assets as recorded was $4,100,000. Kite Co also had an internally generated brand, not recorded by Kite Co, reliably valued at $700,000, and a customer list that cannot be measured reliably.
  • On 1 July 20X6 it bought a regional broadcasting licence for $2,000,000 with a 5-year life. Such licences are freely traded in an active market and Harlow Co uses the revaluation model for them. At 30 June 20X7 the licence's fair value was $1,900,000.
  • It spent $150,000 training editorial staff on new editing software.
What revaluation surplus should be recognised in other comprehensive income for the broadcasting licence for the year ended 30 June 20X7? Enter your answer in $, to the nearest whole number.
ex:
Amortisation = 2,000,000 / 5 = 400,000
Carrying amount before revaluation = 2,000,000 − 400,000 = 1,600,000
Revaluation surplus = 1,900,000 − 1,600,000 = $300,000 (OCI). E'tibor bering: fair value cost'dan past bo'lsa ham, carrying amount'dan yuqori — demak surplus.

q:
Harlow Co, a media company, prepares financial statements to 30 June 20X7. During the year:
  • On 1 July 20X6 it bought a magazine publishing title from a competitor for $1,200,000; useful life 10 years.
  • A consultant has valued Harlow Co's own newspaper masthead, created by Harlow Co over 30 years, at $3 million.
  • On 1 July 20X6 it acquired 100% of Kite Co for $5,600,000. The fair value of Kite Co's identifiable net assets as recorded was $4,100,000. Kite Co also had an internally generated brand, not recorded by Kite Co, reliably valued at $700,000, and a customer list that cannot be measured reliably.
  • On 1 July 20X6 it bought a regional broadcasting licence for $2,000,000 with a 5-year life. Such licences are freely traded in an active market and Harlow Co uses the revaluation model for them. At 30 June 20X7 the licence's fair value was $1,900,000.
  • It spent $150,000 training editorial staff on new editing software.
The $150,000 spent training editorial staff should be expensed to profit or loss.
ex: To'g'ri. Training xarajatlari — entity xodimlarni control qila olmaydi (ular ketishi mumkin), shuning uchun intangible asset ta'rifiga mos kelmaydi → P/L expense.

q: Which of the following would be classified as an investment property under IAS 40 Investment Property?
opt: Land held by Ravelle Co for a currently undetermined future use
A building occupied by Ravelle Co's own sales and marketing staff
A block of flats being built by Ravelle Co under contract for a housing association
Houses completed by Ravelle Co, a property developer, and held for sale in the ordinary course of business
ex:
IAS 40: investment property — ijara daromadi (rentals) yoki capital appreciation uchun ushlab turilgan yer/bino. Kelajakdagi foydalanishi hali aniqlanmagan yer — IAS 40 bo'yicha investment property deb qaraladi (u capital appreciation uchun ushlab turilgan deb hisoblanadi).
• O'z xodimlari ishlatadigan bino — owner-occupied → IAS 16 PPE.
• Mijoz uchun shartnoma asosida qurilayotgan bino — IFRS 15 (revenue from contracts).
• Developer oddiy biznesda sotish uchun ushlab turgan uylar — inventory (IAS 2).

q: Which of the following properties owned by Castlemore Co would NOT be classified as an investment property?
opt: An office building that Castlemore Co leases to an unrelated company under an operating lease
A vacant warehouse that Castlemore Co holds in order to lease it out under operating leases
A hotel which Castlemore Co owns and operates itself, providing cleaning, catering and reception services to guests
Land that Castlemore Co holds for long-term capital appreciation
ex:
Entity o'zi boshqaradigan mehmonxona — xizmatlar (ovqat, tozalash, qabul) significant, ya'ni daromad bino ijarasidan emas, balki biznes faoliyatidan keladi. Shuning uchun u owner-occupied → IAS 16 PPE.
Qolgan uchtasi investment property: operating lease'da berilgan ofis, ijaraga berish uchun ushlab turilgan bo'sh ombor (vacant building held to be leased) va capital appreciation uchun yer.

q: A building owned by Fernhill Co and leased to an unrelated third party under an operating lease is an investment property of Fernhill Co.
ex: To'g'ri. Bino rentals (ijara daromadi) olish uchun ushlab turilibdi va entity uni o'zi ishlatmayapti → IAS 40 investment property.

q: Staff accommodation owned by Dunmore Co, which is occupied by Dunmore Co's employees who pay a market rent, is an investment property of Dunmore Co.
ex: Noto'g'ri. Xodimlar egallagan bino — ular market rent to'lasa ham — owner-occupied property hisoblanadi (entity faoliyati uchun ishlatiladi). Shuning uchun IAS 16 PPE, investment property emas.

q: Which THREE of the following would be classified as investment property in the financial statements of Oakridge Co?
opt: A building under construction by Oakridge Co on behalf of a customer
Land purchased by Oakridge Co to benefit from expected increases in its value
A vacant building held by Oakridge Co to be leased out under operating leases
A retail unit held by Oakridge Co, a property developer, for sale in the ordinary course of business
An office block owned by Oakridge Co and let to several tenants under operating leases
ex:
Investment property: (1) capital appreciation uchun sotib olingan yer; (2) operating lease'ga berish uchun ushlab turilgan bo'sh bino; (3) tenantlarga ijaraga berilgan ofis bloki.
Mijoz nomidan qurilayotgan bino — IFRS 15 (shartnoma). Oddiy biznesda sotish uchun ushlab turilgan retail unit — IAS 2 inventory.

q: Norfield Co owns a five-storey building. It occupies two floors as its head office and lets the other three floors to unrelated tenants under operating leases. Each floor could be sold separately. How should the building be accounted for?
opt: The whole building as investment property, as the majority of floors are let
Two floors as property, plant and equipment under IAS 16 and three floors as investment property under IAS 40
The whole building as property, plant and equipment, as Norfield Co occupies part of it
The whole building as inventory until the tenancies end
ex: Dual-use property: agar qismlarni alohida sotish (yoki finance lease'ga berish) mumkin bo'lsa, ular alohida hisobga olinadi. Norfield egallagan 2 qavat → IAS 16 PPE; ijaraga berilgan 3 qavat → IAS 40 investment property.

q: Pellow Co owns a building which it lets to tenants. Pellow Co uses 4% of the floor space as a small administrative office for managing the building. The parts of the building cannot be sold or leased separately. How should the building be classified?
opt: The whole building is property, plant and equipment, as part of it is owner-occupied
96% as investment property and 4% as property, plant and equipment
The building must be classified as inventory
The whole building is investment property, as the owner-occupied portion is insignificant
ex: Qismlarni alohida sotib bo'lmasa, bino faqat owner-occupied qismi insignificant (juda kichik) bo'lsa investment property bo'ladi. 4% — ahamiyatsiz, shuning uchun butun bino IAS 40 bo'yicha investment property. Bo'lib hisoblash (96%/4%) faqat qismlar alohida sotilishi mumkin bo'lganda qo'llanadi.

q: Brackwell Co is a property developer. Which THREE of the following should Brackwell Co classify as investment property?
opt: An office block let to tenants under operating leases to earn rentals
Apartments built by Brackwell Co which are being marketed for sale to the public
Land held by Brackwell Co for which the future use has not yet been decided
A building used by Brackwell Co as its own head office
A newly completed building which is currently vacant but is held to be let under operating leases
ex:
Developer bo'lsa ham, klassifikatsiya maqsadga bog'liq:
• Ijaraga berilgan ofis bloki → IP.
• Kelajakdagi foydalanishi aniqlanmagan yer → IP.
• Ijaraga berish uchun ushlab turilgan bo'sh bino → IP.
• Sotish uchun marketing qilinayotgan kvartiralar → IAS 2 inventory (oddiy biznes faoliyati).
• O'z head office → IAS 16 PPE.

q: If an entity chooses the fair value model under IAS 40, it must apply that model to all of its investment properties.
ex: To'g'ri. IAS 40 accounting policy tanlovini beradi (cost model yoki fair value model), lekin tanlangan model barcha investment property'larga qo'llanishi kerak.

q: Which of the following best explains why IAS 40 permits investment properties to be measured at fair value with no depreciation charged?
opt: Investment properties generate cash flows largely independently of the entity's other assets, so their current value and changes in that value are the most relevant information for users
Buildings held as investments do not suffer any physical wear and tear
Tax authorities do not allow depreciation on investment properties
Fair value is always lower than depreciated cost, so the fair value model is more prudent
ex: Investment property korxona operatsiyalarida ishlatilmaydi — u investitsiya sifatida (rentals yoki capital growth) ushlab turiladi. Foydalanuvchilar uchun eng muhim ma'lumot — uning joriy qiymati va qiymat o'zgarishi. Depreciation esa 'aktivni ishlatish orqali iste'mol qilish'ni aks ettiradi — investitsiya uchun bu unchalik ma'noli emas. Boshqa variantlar noto'g'ri: binolar eskiradi, soliq qoidalari IFRS'ni belgilamaydi, FV har doim past emas.

q: Hollin Co owns an office building which it leases at a market rent to its wholly owned subsidiary, Sparrow Co. Sparrow Co uses the building as its head office. How should the building be classified?
opt: Investment property in both Hollin Co's individual and the consolidated financial statements
Property, plant and equipment in Hollin Co's individual financial statements; investment property in the consolidated financial statements
Property, plant and equipment in both Hollin Co's individual and the consolidated financial statements
Investment property in Hollin Co's individual financial statements; property, plant and equipment in the consolidated financial statements
ex: Hollin'ning individual FS'ida bino boshqa yuridik shaxsga ijaraga berilgan → investment property. Consolidated FS'da esa guruh bitta entity (single entity concept) va binoni guruhning o'zi (Sparrow) ishlatadi → owner-occupied → IAS 16 PPE.

q: In consolidated financial statements, a building owned by a subsidiary and let to its parent company for use as the parent's head office is classified as investment property.
ex: Noto'g'ri. Guruh nuqtai nazaridan binoni guruhning bir a'zosi (parent) ishlatadi — bu owner-occupied. Consolidated FS'da u IAS 16 PPE bo'ladi (subsidiary'ning individual FS'ida esa IP bo'lishi mumkin).

q:
Ardent Co purchased a building for $6,000,000 on 1 January 20X4 and immediately leased it to its subsidiary, Birch Co, which uses it as a factory. The building has a useful life of 40 years (ignore land). Ardent Co uses the fair value model for investment property and the cost model for property, plant and equipment. The fair value of the building at 31 December 20X4 was $6,600,000.
At what amount should the building be shown in the consolidated statement of financial position at 31 December 20X4?
ex:
Consolidated FS'da bino guruh tomonidan ishlatiladi → IAS 16 PPE (cost model), depreciation olinadi.
Depreciation = 6,000,000 / 40 = 150,000
Carrying amount = 6,000,000 − 150,000 = $5,850,000.
(Ardent'ning individual FS'ida esa IP sifatida FV $6,600,000 da ko'rsatiladi, gain 600,000 P/L'ga.)

q: How should an investment property be measured on initial recognition under IAS 40?
opt: At fair value less costs to sell
At fair value, with any difference from the price paid taken to profit or loss
At cost, including directly attributable transaction costs
At the purchase price only, with legal fees expensed
ex: IAS 40: investment property dastlab costda o'lchanadi — sotib olish narxi + to'g'ridan-to'g'ri bog'liq xarajatlar (legal fees, property transfer taxes, professional fees). Keyin (subsequent measurement) cost model yoki fair value model tanlanadi.

q:
Wexford Co acquired an office building to hold as an investment property. The following costs were incurred:
Purchase price$4,200,000
Legal fees on the purchase$85,000
Property transfer tax$126,000
Allocation of Wexford Co's general administrative overheads$40,000
At what amount should the investment property be initially recognised? Enter your answer in $, to the nearest whole dollar.
ex:
Dastlabki cost = purchase price + directly attributable costs.
4,200,000 + 85,000 (legal) + 126,000 (transfer tax) = $4,411,000.
Umumiy admin overheads (40,000) to'g'ridan-to'g'ri bog'liq emas → expense.

q: Which THREE of the following costs should be included in the initial cost of an investment property?
opt: Operating losses incurred before the property reaches its planned level of occupancy
Legal fees incurred on the purchase
Property transfer taxes
Start-up costs of advertising the property to potential tenants
Professional surveyor's fees for the purchase
ex:
Initial cost'ga faqat directly attributable xarajatlar kiradi: legal fees, property transfer taxes, professional fees.
IAS 40 aniq ta'kidlaydi: start-up costs, rejalashtirilgan occupancy darajasiga yetguncha bo'lgan operating losses va g'ayrioddiy isrof (abnormal waste) cost'ga kirmaydi → expense.

q: Under the fair value model in IAS 40, how are changes in the fair value of investment property recognised?
opt: In profit or loss, with depreciation charged on the fair value
In other comprehensive income, with no depreciation charged
In profit or loss, with no depreciation charged
In other comprehensive income, with depreciation charged on the fair value
ex: Fair value model: har yil oxirida FV'ga qayta o'lchanadi, gain yoki loss profit or lossga (OCI emas!) va depreciation olinmaydi. Bu IAS 16 revaluation model'dan asosiy farq (u yerda surplus OCI'ga va depreciation davom etadi).

q:
Linford Co purchased a property for $5,000,000 on 1 January 20X5 to earn rental income. Linford Co uses the fair value model for investment property. At 31 December 20X5 the fair value of the property was $5,450,000.
What gain should be recognised in profit or loss for the year ended 31 December 20X5? Enter your answer in $000, to the nearest whole number.
ex:
Fair value model: gain = FV yil oxiri − oldingi carrying amount (bu yerda cost).
5,450,000 − 5,000,000 = 450,000 → 450 ($000). Depreciation yo'q.

q:
On 1 January 20X6 Morland Co paid $7,500,000 for an office block, which it holds to earn rentals. The block has an estimated useful life of 30 years. Morland Co measures investment property using the fair value model. At 31 December 20X6 an independent valuer assessed the fair value of the block at $8,100,000; agents' fees of $150,000 would be incurred if it were sold.
What gain should be recognised in profit or loss for the year ended 31 December 20X6?
ex:
Fair value model'da aktiv fair valueda o'lchanadi — costs to sell ayirilmaydi (bu IFRS 5 yoki IAS 41 emas). Depreciation ham olinmaydi.
Gain = 8,100,000 − 7,500,000 = $600,000.

q:
Thornby Co bought a property for $2,400,000 (including land of $600,000) on 1 January 20X6 to lease to tenants. The building has a useful life of 40 years. The fair value of the property at 31 December 20X6 was $2,520,000. Thornby Co uses the fair value model.
What is the effect on profit or loss for the year ended 31 December 20X6?
opt: Gain of $120,000 and no depreciation
No gain in profit or loss; $120,000 is recognised in other comprehensive income
Gain of $165,000 and depreciation of $45,000
Depreciation of $45,000 only
ex:
Fair value model: depreciation olinmaydi, FV o'zgarishi P/L'ga.
Gain = 2,520,000 − 2,400,000 = $120,000.
Chalg'ituvchi javoblar depreciation (1,800,000/40 = 45,000) yoki OCI'ni ishlatadi — bular IAS 16 ga tegishli.

q:
Galloway Co holds an office block as an investment property under the fair value model. Its fair value was $9,200,000 at 31 March 20X7 and $8,750,000 at 31 March 20X8. Rental income of $520,000 was earned in the year ended 31 March 20X8.
What is the net effect of the property on profit or loss for the year ended 31 March 20X8? Enter your answer in $000 as a positive number for net income or a negative number for a net expense.
Under the IAS 40 fair value model, a decrease in the fair value of an investment property that was previously revalued upwards is first charged against a revaluation surplus in equity.
ex: Noto'g'ri. Fair value model'da revaluation surplus yo'q — barcha o'sish va pasayishlar to'g'ridan-to'g'ri profit or lossga. Surplus'ga qarshi yozish IAS 16 revaluation model qoidasi.

q: Which THREE of the following statements about the IAS 40 fair value model are correct?
opt: No depreciation is charged on the investment property
Gains and losses arising from changes in fair value are recognised in profit or loss
Gains arising from changes in fair value are recognised in other comprehensive income
The model must be applied to all of the entity's investment properties
An entity may switch freely between the fair value and cost models from year to year
ex:
To'g'ri: depreciation yo'q; FV o'zgarishlari P/L'ga; model barcha IP'larga qo'llanadi.
Noto'g'ri: OCI — bu IAS 16 revaluation; model'ni har yili o'zgartirib bo'lmaydi — o'zgartirish faqat IAS 8 bo'yicha, agar u yanada mos (more appropriate) taqdimotga olib kelsa.

q:
Kelso Co purchased an investment property on 1 July 20X3 for $3,200,000. Kelso Co's year end is 31 December and it uses the fair value model. The fair value of the property was $3,350,000 at 31 December 20X3 and $3,280,000 at 31 December 20X4.
What amount should be recognised in profit or loss for the year ended 31 December 20X4 in respect of the change in fair value?
opt: Gain of $80,000
Nil in profit or loss; a loss of $70,000 in other comprehensive income
Gain of $150,000
Loss of $70,000
ex:
20X4 yilgi o'zgarish = yil boshidagi FV bilan yil oxiridagi FV farqi (cost bilan emas).
3,280,000 − 3,350,000 = −70,000 → loss $70,000 P/L'ga.
(20X3 da gain 150,000 allaqachon tan olingan.)

q: Under the IAS 40 cost model, how is an investment property measured after initial recognition?
opt: At cost less accumulated depreciation and impairment losses, in line with IAS 16, with fair value disclosed in the notes
At fair value, with changes recognised in other comprehensive income
At cost, with no depreciation charged
At fair value less costs to sell
ex: Cost model = IAS 16 cost model: cost − accumulated depreciation − impairment. IAS 40 bu holda ham investment property'ning fair valuesini izohlarda (notes) oshkor qilishni talab qiladi.

q:
Radley Co purchased a property for $1,800,000 on 1 January 20X7 to let to tenants. The land element is $500,000 and the building has a useful life of 40 years with no residual value. Radley Co uses the cost model for investment property.
What is the carrying amount of the property at 31 December 20X8? Enter your answer in $, to the nearest whole dollar.
ex:
Cost model → IAS 16 kabi depreciation. Yer (land) depreciation qilinmaydi.
Yillik depreciation = (1,800,000 − 500,000) / 40 = 32,500
2 yil (20X7, 20X8): 2 × 32,500 = 65,000
Carrying amount = 1,800,000 − 65,000 = $1,735,000.

q:
Radley Co purchased a property for $1,800,000 on 1 January 20X7 to let to tenants. The land element is $500,000 and the building has a useful life of 40 years with no residual value. The fair value of the property at 31 December 20X7 was $1,950,000.
By how much would profit for the year ended 31 December 20X7 be higher under the fair value model than under the cost model? Enter your answer in $, to the nearest whole dollar.
ex:
Fair value model: gain = 1,950,000 − 1,800,000 = +150,000, depreciation yo'q.
Cost model: depreciation = (1,800,000 − 500,000) / 40 = −32,500, gain yo'q.
Farq = 150,000 + 32,500 = $182,500.

q:
Hamble Co purchased an investment property on 1 January 20X1 for $6,000,000. The property had a useful life of 40 years with no residual value (ignore land). At 31 December 20X3 its fair value was $6,900,000. On 1 January 20X4 the property was sold for net proceeds of $6,750,000.
What is the profit or loss on disposal under the cost model and under the fair value model?
opt: Cost model: profit $750,000; fair value model: loss $150,000
Cost model: profit $1,200,000; fair value model: loss $150,000
Cost model: profit $1,200,000; fair value model: profit $750,000
Cost model: profit $750,000; fair value model: profit $750,000
ex:
Disposal gain/loss = net proceeds − carrying amount.
Cost model: 3 yil depreciation = 3 × 6,000,000/40 = 450,000; CA = 5,550,000; profit = 6,750,000 − 5,550,000 = 1,200,000.
FV model: CA = oxirgi FV 6,900,000; loss = 6,750,000 − 6,900,000 = −150,000.

q: An investment property measured under the IAS 40 cost model is depreciated over its useful life (except for any land element).
ex: To'g'ri. Cost model IAS 16 cost model'ga amal qiladi: bino qismi useful life davomida depreciation qilinadi, yer odatda depreciation qilinmaydi.

q: Which TWO of the following statements about the IAS 40 cost model are correct?
opt: The fair value of the investment property must be disclosed in the notes
Increases in fair value are recognised in other comprehensive income
The property is depreciated in accordance with IAS 16
An entity may use the cost model for some investment properties and the fair value model for others
ex:
To'g'ri: cost model'da ham FV notesda oshkor qilinadi; bino IAS 16 bo'yicha depreciation qilinadi.
Noto'g'ri: FV o'zgarishlari cost model'da umuman tan olinmaydi (OCI ham emas); tanlangan model barcha IP'larga qo'llanadi.

q: An owner-occupied property is transferred to investment property. The entity uses the fair value model for investment property. How should the transfer be accounted for?
opt: Revalue the property to fair value at the date of change in use, with the gain taken to profit or loss
Transfer the property at its carrying amount and remeasure it to fair value at the year end, with the whole gain in profit or loss
Revalue the property to fair value under IAS 16 at the date of change in use, with the gain taken to other comprehensive income, then transfer it to investment property at fair value
Transfer the property at its original cost and stop depreciating it
ex: PPE → IP (FV model): aktiv o'tkazish sanasigacha hali PPE, shuning uchun IAS 16 revaluation qoidalari qo'llanadi: avval o'sha sanagacha depreciation, keyin FV'ga revaluation, surplus OCIga (revaluation surplus). Shundan keyin aktiv IP sifatida FV'da; keyingi FV o'zgarishlari P/L'ga.

q:
Glenmore Co's head office had a carrying amount of $4,800,000 on 1 January 20X6, with a remaining useful life of 24 years. On 1 July 20X6 Glenmore Co vacated the building and let it to an unrelated tenant. The fair value was $5,300,000 at 1 July 20X6 and $5,420,000 at 31 December 20X6. Glenmore Co uses the fair value model for investment property.
What amount should be credited to the revaluation surplus (other comprehensive income) for the year ended 31 December 20X6? Enter your answer in $, to the nearest whole dollar.
ex:
1) 1 Jan–30 Jun: PPE, depreciation = 4,800,000/24 × 6/12 = 100,000
2) CA at 1 July = 4,800,000 − 100,000 = 4,700,000
3) IAS 16 revaluation: 5,300,000 − 4,700,000 = 600,000 → OCI (revaluation surplus).
(1 Jul–31 Dec o'sish 120,000 esa P/L'ga ketadi.)

q:
Glenmore Co's head office had a carrying amount of $4,800,000 on 1 January 20X6, with a remaining useful life of 24 years. On 1 July 20X6 Glenmore Co vacated the building and let it to an unrelated tenant. The fair value was $5,300,000 at 1 July 20X6 and $5,420,000 at 31 December 20X6. Glenmore Co uses the fair value model for investment property.
Ignoring rental income, what is the net effect of the building on profit or loss for the year ended 31 December 20X6?
opt: Net income of $120,000
Net income of $620,000
Net income of $720,000
Net income of $20,000
ex:
P/L'ga ketadigan narsalar:
• 6 oylik depreciation (PPE davrida): −100,000
• IP bo'lgandan keyingi FV gain: 5,420,000 − 5,300,000 = +120,000
Net = 120,000 − 100,000 = 20,000.
Transfer sanasidagi surplus 600,000 OCI'ga ketadi, P/L'ga emas.

q:
On 1 January 20X2 Ashby Co acquired a building for $8,000,000 for use as its own administrative headquarters (ignore land). The building was depreciated straight-line over 40 years with no residual value. On 1 April 20X4 Ashby Co relocated its staff and leased the building to an unrelated tenant. Ashby Co uses the fair value model for investment property. The fair value of the building was $8,900,000 at 1 April 20X4 and $9,250,000 at 31 December 20X4.
Ignoring rental income, what is the net amount recognised in profit or loss for the year ended 31 December 20X4 in respect of the building?
opt: Net income of $1,650,000
Net income of $350,000
Net income of $300,000
Net income of $1,700,000

q: An owner-occupied building is let to a third party and reclassified as investment property. The entity uses the cost model for investment property. How is the transfer accounted for?
opt: The property is revalued to fair value with the gain in other comprehensive income
The property is transferred at its carrying amount and depreciation stops
The property is revalued to fair value with the gain in profit or loss
The property is transferred at its carrying amount and continues to be depreciated
ex: Cost model'da transfer carrying amountda amalga oshadi — cost, accumulated depreciation va o'lchov o'zgarmaydi. Depreciation qolgan useful life davomida davom etadi; fair value ahamiyatsiz (faqat notes'da oshkor qilinadi).

q:
Pemberton Co's office building had a carrying amount of $3,600,000 at 1 April 20X5 and a remaining useful life of 18 years. On 1 October 20X5 it was let to a third party and reclassified as investment property, when its fair value was $3,900,000. At 31 March 20X6 its fair value was $4,050,000. Pemberton Co uses the cost model for investment property.
What is the carrying amount of the building at 31 March 20X6? Enter your answer in $000, to the nearest whole number.
ex:
Cost model: transfer carrying amount'da, fair value e'tiborga olinmaydi.
To'liq yil depreciation (6 oy PPE + 6 oy IP) = 3,600,000/18 = 200,000
CA = 3,600,000 − 200,000 = 3,400,000 → 3,400 ($000).

q: When an owner-occupied property is transferred to investment property carried under the fair value model, the revaluation gain arising at the date of transfer is recognised in profit or loss.
ex: Noto'g'ri. Transfer sanasigacha aktiv PPE, shuning uchun o'sha sanadagi revaluation IAS 16 bo'yicha — gain OCIga (revaluation surplus). Faqat transferdan keyingi FV o'zgarishlari P/L'ga.

q: An entity transfers an owner-occupied building to investment property and uses the fair value model. Which THREE of the following statements are correct?
opt: The revaluation surplus arising on transfer is reclassified to profit or loss when the property is later sold
Depreciation is charged up to the date of the change in use
The gain on revaluation at the date of transfer is recognised in other comprehensive income
No depreciation is charged at all in the year of transfer
Changes in fair value after the date of transfer are recognised in profit or loss
ex:
To'g'ri: change in use sanasigacha depreciation olinadi; o'sha sanadagi revaluation gain OCI'ga; transferdan keyingi FV o'zgarishlari P/L'ga.
Noto'g'ri: revaluation surplus P/L'ga reclassify qilinmaydi (sotilganda retained earnings'ga to'g'ridan-to'g'ri o'tkazilishi mumkin); transfer yilida PPE davri uchun depreciation olinadi.

q: An investment property carried under the fair value model becomes owner-occupied. How should the change in use be accounted for?
opt: Remeasure to fair value at the date of change in use, with the gain in other comprehensive income, and stop depreciating
Remeasure to fair value at the date of change in use, with the gain or loss in profit or loss; that fair value becomes the deemed cost for IAS 16 and is depreciated thereafter
Transfer at the property's original purchase cost and depreciate from that amount
Transfer at the fair value at the previous year end, with no remeasurement at the date of change
ex: IP → PPE (FV model): o'tkazishdan oldin aktiv hali IP, shuning uchun IAS 40 qoidasi: FV'ga qayta o'lchash, gain/loss P/Lga. Shu FV — IAS 16 uchun deemed cost; keyin qolgan useful life davomida depreciation.

q:
Harlow Co carries an investment property under the fair value model. Its fair value at 1 January 20X7 was $7,200,000. On 1 April 20X7 Harlow Co moved its own staff into the property and began using it as its head office. The fair value at that date was $7,650,000 and the remaining useful life was 30 years.
What is the net effect of the property on Harlow Co's profit or loss for the year ended 31 December 20X7? Enter your answer in $ as a positive number for net income or a negative number for a net expense.

Harlow Co carries an investment property under the fair value model. Its fair value at 1 January 20X7 was $7,200,000. On 1 April 20X7 Harlow Co began using the property as its head office, when its fair value was $7,650,000 and its remaining useful life was 30 years. At 31 December 20X7 the fair value was $7,800,000. Harlow Co uses the cost model for property, plant and equipment.
Which TWO of the following statements about Harlow Co's financial statements for the year ended 31 December 20X7 are correct?
opt: The property is shown within property, plant and equipment at $7,458,750
A gain of $450,000 is recognised in other comprehensive income
The property is shown as investment property at $7,800,000
A gain of $450,000 is recognised in profit or loss
ex:
1 Apr gacha IP → FV gain 450,000 P/Lga (OCI emas).
1 Apr dan PPE: deemed cost 7,650,000, depreciation 7,650,000/30 × 9/12 = 191,250; yil oxiridagi CA = 7,650,000 − 191,250 = 7,458,750.
31 Dec dagi FV $7,800,000 ahamiyatsiz — bino endi IP emas (va IAS 16 cost model qo'llanadi).

q:
Ludlow Co, a property developer, holds a completed building in inventory at a cost of $2,100,000. On 1 May 20X8 Ludlow Co grants an operating lease of the building to a third party and will hold it to earn rentals. The fair value of the building at that date is $2,600,000. Ludlow Co uses the fair value model for investment property.
How should the transfer be accounted for?
opt: Transfer to investment property at $2,600,000 with a gain of $500,000 in profit or loss
Transfer to investment property at $2,600,000 with a gain of $500,000 in other comprehensive income
The building remains in inventory until it is sold
Transfer to investment property at $2,100,000, with no gain recognised
ex:
Inventory → IP (FV model): operating lease'ning boshlanishi — change in use dalili. Aktiv FV'da IP'ga o'tkaziladi va FV bilan oldingi carrying amount orasidagi farq P/Lga (xuddi inventory sotilgandek).
Gain = 2,600,000 − 2,100,000 = 500,000.

q: Lanark Co holds an investment property under the fair value model. It begins redeveloping the property with a view to selling it in the ordinary course of business. How should this be accounted for?
opt: Transfer the property to inventory at its original purchase cost
Transfer the property to inventory, using its fair value at the date of change in use as deemed cost
Transfer the property to inventory at fair value less costs to sell, with the difference in other comprehensive income
Continue to carry the property as investment property until it is sold
ex: IP → inventory: change in use dalili — sotish maqsadida development boshlanishi. FV model'da aktiv o'sha sanadagi FVga qayta o'lchanib (farq P/L'ga), shu FV IAS 2 uchun deemed cost bo'ladi. Agar development bo'lmasa va shunchaki sotilsa, u sotilguncha IP bo'lib qoladi.

q: A decision by management to sell an investment property without any redevelopment is, on its own, sufficient for the property to be transferred to inventory.
ex: Noto'g'ri. IAS 40: transfer faqat change in use dalili bo'lganda. Faqat niyat (management intention) yetarli emas. Development'siz sotiladigan IP sotilguncha (derecognition) IP bo'lib qoladi — IFRS 5 held for sale shartlari bajarilsa ham, FV model'dagi IP IFRS 5 measurement'dan ozod.

q:
Tallis Co, a property developer, held a block of apartments in inventory at a cost of $3,840,000. On 1 March 20X8 it leased the whole block to a housing company under an operating lease and now holds it to earn rentals. The fair value of the block was $4,350,000 at 1 March 20X8 and $4,470,000 at 31 December 20X8. Tallis Co uses the fair value model for investment property.
What is the total gain recognised in profit or loss for the year ended 31 December 20X8 in respect of the block? Enter your answer in $000, to the nearest whole number.
IAS 40 requires a transfer to or from investment property only when there is evidence of a change in use. Which THREE of the following are examples of such evidence?
opt: A significant rise in local property prices
Commencement of owner-occupation
Commencement of development with a view to sale
A board resolution stating that the property may be sold in the future
Inception of an operating lease to another party of a property previously held as inventory
ex: Change in use dalillari: owner-occupation boshlanishi (IP → PPE); sotish uchun development boshlanishi (IP → inventory); boshqa tomonga operating lease boshlanishi (inventory → IP). Narxlarning o'sishi yoki faqat management niyati — change in use emas.

q:
Corbin Co carries an investment property under the fair value model. At 31 December 20X5 its fair value was $5,600,000. On 1 March 20X6 Corbin Co sold the property for $5,950,000 and incurred selling costs of $95,000. There was no change in fair value between 31 December 20X5 and the date of sale.
What is the gain on disposal? Enter your answer in $000, to the nearest whole number.
ex:
Gain = net disposal proceeds − carrying amount.
Net proceeds = 5,950,000 − 95,000 = 5,855,000
Gain = 5,855,000 − 5,600,000 = 255,000 → 255 ($000), P/L'ga.

q:
Selby Co purchased an investment property on 1 October 20X2 for $2,700,000, including land of $900,000. The building had a useful life of 36 years. Selby Co uses the cost model and has a 30 September year end. On 30 September 20X6 the property was sold for $3,100,000 (no selling costs), when its fair value was $3,150,000.
What is the profit on disposal? Enter your answer in $, to the nearest whole dollar.
Drayton Co recognised a fair value gain of $300,000 on its investment property during the year. How is this gain dealt with in Drayton Co's statement of cash flows prepared using the indirect method?
opt: Added to profit before tax in cash flows from operating activities
Shown as a cash inflow in investing activities
Deducted from profit before tax in cash flows from operating activities
Shown as a cash inflow in financing activities
ex: FV gain — non-cash daromad. U profit before tax ichida, lekin pul kelmagan → indirect method'da operating activities'da ayiriladi. IP sotib olish/sotish pul oqimlari investing activities'da.

q: Which THREE of the following are correct presentations for an entity that holds investment property under the fair value model?
opt: Fair value gains are presented in other comprehensive income
Rental income is recognised in profit or loss
Fair value gains are recognised in profit or loss
Investment property is presented within inventories
Cash paid to purchase investment property is an investing cash outflow
ex:
To'g'ri: rental income P/L'da; FV gain P/L'da; IP xaridi SOCF'da investing activities.
Noto'g'ri: FV gain OCI'da emas; IP — non-current asset, inventory emas.

q:
Extracts from Farrow Co's statements of financial position show investment property (fair value model) of $14,200,000 at 1 January 20X9 and $16,050,000 at 31 December 20X9. During the year a fair value gain of $650,000 was recognised and a property with a fair value of $1,300,000 was transferred to property, plant and equipment on becoming owner-occupied. There were no disposals.
What cash was paid to acquire investment property during the year? Enter your answer in $000, to the nearest whole number.
ex:
IP T-hisobi ($000):
Opening 14,200 + FV gain 650 − PPE'ga transfer 1,300 + xarid X = closing 16,050
X = 16,050 − 14,200 − 650 + 1,300 = 2,500 (investing outflow).

q: Which of the following measurement models are permitted by IAS 40 for investment properties after initial recognition?
opt: The cost model and the fair value model only
The revaluation model and the fair value model only
The cost model, the revaluation model and the fair value model
The cost model and the revaluation model only
ex: IAS 40 faqat ikki model: cost model va fair value model. Revaluation model (surplus OCI'ga, depreciation davom etadi) — IAS 16 PPE va IAS 38 uchun, IP uchun emas.

q:
Tamarind Co prepares financial statements to 31 December 20X7 and uses the fair value model for investment property. It has an 80% subsidiary, Lotus Co.
Property X: Tamarind Co's head office had a carrying amount of $6,300,000 at 1 January 20X7 and a remaining useful life of 35 years. On 1 May 20X7 Tamarind Co moved its staff out and let the building to an unrelated tenant. Its fair value was $6,900,000 at 1 May 20X7 and $7,050,000 at 31 December 20X7.
Property Y: A warehouse let to Lotus Co, which uses it to store its inventory. Its fair value was $2,400,000 at 1 January 20X7 and $2,280,000 at 31 December 20X7.
Property Z: Land purchased on 1 March 20X7 for $1,500,000 plus legal fees of $30,000. The directors have not yet decided how the land will be used. Its fair value at 31 December 20X7 was $1,620,000.

What amount should be recognised in other comprehensive income in respect of Property X for the year ended 31 December 20X7? Enter your answer in $, to the nearest whole dollar.

Tamarind Co prepares financial statements to 31 December 20X7 and uses the fair value model for investment property. It has an 80% subsidiary, Lotus Co.
Property X: Tamarind Co's head office had a carrying amount of $6,300,000 at 1 January 20X7 and a remaining useful life of 35 years. On 1 May 20X7 Tamarind Co moved its staff out and let the building to an unrelated tenant. Its fair value was $6,900,000 at 1 May 20X7 and $7,050,000 at 31 December 20X7.

What is the net fair value gain on investment properties to be recognised in Tamarind Co's individual statement of profit or loss for the year ended 31 December 20X7? Enter your answer in $, to the nearest whole dollar.

Property X: Tamarind Co's head office had a carrying amount of $6,300,000 at 1 January 20X7 and a remaining useful life of 35 years. On 1 May 20X7 Tamarind Co moved its staff out and let the building to an unrelated tenant. Its fair value was $6,900,000 at 1 May 20X7 and $7,050,000 at 31 December 20X7.

Property Z: Land purchased on 1 March 20X7 for $1,500,000 plus legal fees of $30,000. The directors have not yet decided how the land will be used. Its fair value at 31 December 20X7 was $1,620,000.

How should Property Y be treated in the consolidated financial statements of the Tamarind group?
opt: As investment property under the cost model
As investment property at its fair value of $2,280,000
It is eliminated entirely as an intra-group item
As property, plant and equipment under IAS 16, because it is used by the group
